title: Architectural Glossary
subtitle: Explaining architectural terms in a language everyone can understand.

terms.definition: A vaulted (arch-ceilinged) passage built over a street, linking the houses on both sides. It is typical of the old town fabric of Mardin and south-eastern Turkey.
terms.simple_definition: A covered, arched passage built over a street that joins the houses on either side.

terms.definition: A ceiling made of, or covered with, sound-absorbing panels. It cuts down echo and background noise so that speech in the room sounds clearer.
terms.simple_definition: A ceiling that soaks up echo and makes a room quieter.

terms.definition: A panel fixed to a wall or ceiling that absorbs sound and reduces echo. It is usually made of fabric-covered mineral wool, felt, wooden slats or special foam.
terms.simple_definition: A panel hung on a wall to reduce echo and soften the sound in a room.

terms.definition: The science of how sound travels, bounces and is absorbed in a space; in architecture it is used to design rooms that sound clear and are free of unwanted noise.
terms.simple_definition: How sound behaves in a room, and how to make it sound better.

terms.definition: How strongly two materials grip each other; especially how well concrete grips the steel bars (rebar) inside it. Poor bond lets the bars slip out of the concrete.
terms.simple_definition: How tightly concrete holds on to the steel bars inside it.

terms.definition: How pleasing a building or space looks and feels, through the harmony of its shapes, proportions, colours and materials.
terms.simple_definition: How beautiful and well put together a building or room looks.

terms.definition: An artificial stone slab made by binding crushed marble or quartz with resin and pressing it. It is used for kitchen worktops, bathrooms and flooring.
terms.simple_definition: Man-made stone made from crushed stone and glue, often used for kitchen countertops.

terms.definition: The sand, gravel and crushed stone mixed into concrete, mortar and asphalt. It makes up most of the mix and gives it strength.
terms.simple_definition: The sand and gravel mixed into concrete.

terms.definition: The open public square of an ancient Greek city, used for markets and gatherings and surrounded by public buildings and covered walkways.
terms.simple_definition: The main market and meeting square of an ancient Greek city.

terms.definition: A narrow space deliberately left between the layers of a wall or behind façade cladding. It lets moisture escape and helps with insulation.
terms.simple_definition: A thin gap left inside a wall to keep it dry and better insulated.

terms.definition: A kitchen layout with no wall between the kitchen and the living room, so both share one space; often a counter or breakfast bar marks the boundary. In Turkey it is commonly called an "American kitchen".
terms.simple_definition: A kitchen that is open to the living room, with no wall between them.

terms.definition: Inspecting, measuring and recording a plot, an existing building or its surroundings before a project starts. Design decisions are based on this information.
terms.simple_definition: Studying and measuring a site before starting the design.

terms.definition: A steel rod, bolt or fixing system used to fasten an element firmly to concrete, a wall or rock. It is common in retaining walls and façade cladding.
terms.simple_definition: A steel fixing that locks something firmly into concrete or a wall.

terms.definition: A self-contained home within a multi-storey building, with its own front door, kitchen and bathroom.
terms.simple_definition: A single home inside a larger building.

terms.definition: A semicircular or polygonal recess, usually covered by a half-dome, at the end of a church or basilica, where the altar typically stands.
terms.simple_definition: The rounded end of a church.

terms.definition: An Ottoman market street, often roofed, where shops of the same trade line both sides. Its rents usually funded a nearby mosque.
terms.simple_definition: An old covered shopping street lined with shops of the same trade.

terms.definition: A light garden structure of posts and a lattice roof, covered with vines or climbing plants to create shade.
terms.simple_definition: A garden shelter covered with climbing plants for shade.

terms.definition: A row of arches resting on columns or piers, often forming a covered walkway alongside a building.
terms.simple_definition: A row of arches sitting on columns.

terms.definition: A curved structure that spans a door, window or passage opening and carries the weight above it down to the supports on each side.
terms.simple_definition: A curved top over an opening that holds up the wall above.

terms.definition: Describes a door, window, passage or building whose top is formed as an arch.
terms.simple_definition: Having a rounded, arch-shaped top.

terms.definition: The profession of designing buildings and their surroundings so they are useful, safe and beautiful, and of guiding how they are built. An architect thinks about room layout, light, materials and appearance together.
terms.simple_definition: The art and job of designing houses and buildings.

terms.definition: In classical architecture, the horizontal stone beam that rests on top of the column capitals and links the columns together.
terms.simple_definition: The stone beam laid across the tops of columns in a classical temple.

terms.definition: The frame-like trim, usually wood or MDF, that covers the joint between a door or window frame and the wall. It hides the gap and also acts as decoration.
terms.simple_definition: The trim strip that frames the edges of a door or window.

terms.definition: An architecture and design style born in France in the 1920s–30s and popular worldwide, known for geometric patterns, stepped forms, glossy materials and elegant ornament.
terms.simple_definition: The glamorous 1920s style with bold geometric patterns.

terms.definition: A black material made by mixing bitumen with sand and gravel, used to surface roads, car parks and some roofs.
terms.simple_definition: The black material used to pave roads.

terms.definition: In ancient Roman houses, an inner court open to the sky; today, a tall, light-filled space several storeys high at the centre of a building, usually under a glass roof.
terms.simple_definition: A tall open space in the middle of a building, often with a glass roof.

terms.definition: The space between the ceiling of the top floor and the roof, usually not fitted out as a living area. It is mostly used for storage and roof insulation.
terms.simple_definition: The space between the top ceiling and the roof where things are stored.

terms.definition: A storey under a pitched roof that is fitted out as a room, office or storage. Its ceiling is usually sloped and low in places because it follows the roof.
terms.simple_definition: A usable top floor tucked under a sloping roof.

terms.definition: Controlling systems such as lighting, heating and cooling, blinds, alarms and doors automatically or from a phone, using sensors and software. In homes it is often called a "smart home".
terms.simple_definition: A system that lets lights, heating or blinds work on their own or from your phone.

terms.definition: An approach in architecture and art that deliberately breaks with tradition to put forward new, experimental and daring ideas.
terms.simple_definition: Bold, experimental design that breaks the usual rules.

terms.definition: A type of 3D technical drawing that shows a building from above and from two sides at once, while keeping its measurements true to scale.
terms.simple_definition: A 3D-looking drawing of a building that keeps the real proportions.

terms.definition: An open platform that projects from a building's façade, is enclosed by a railing and is reached through a door from a room.
terms.simple_definition: A small railed outdoor platform sticking out from a building.

terms.definition: A light timber framing system for houses in which thin, standard-sized studs run continuously through more than one storey and are nailed together. It spread in 19th-century America.
terms.simple_definition: A quick way of building a house frame from thin wooden studs.

terms.definition: A curved roof or ceiling shaped like half a cylinder, formed by one continuous arch. It is used to cover long rooms and corridors.
terms.simple_definition: A long, rounded ceiling shaped like a tunnel.

terms.definition: A ceiling made of a thin PVC or fabric membrane stretched across tracks fixed around the room's edges. It gives a perfectly smooth finish and can be backlit to glow.
terms.simple_definition: A thin sheet stretched tight like a drum across the ceiling, sometimes lit from behind.

terms.definition: A storey of a building that lies wholly or partly below ground level, used for storage, parking, plant rooms or living space.
terms.simple_definition: The floor of a building that is below ground.

terms.definition: A German design school (1919–1933) that brought together art, craft and industrial production; its name became shorthand for plain, functional modern design without ornament.
terms.simple_definition: A famous German school whose name stands for simple, practical, unornamented design.

terms.definition: A traditional Turkish house whose upper floors have enclosed projecting bays (cumba) overhanging the street, bringing in extra light and views.
terms.simple_definition: An old Turkish house with windowed rooms jutting out over the street.

terms.definition: A horizontal structural member spanning between columns or walls that carries the load of the floors and walls above and passes it to the columns. It can be concrete, steel or timber.
terms.simple_definition: A strong horizontal bar that holds up floors and ceilings.

terms.definition: A ceiling where the structural or decorative beams are left exposed rather than hidden. Timber beamed ceilings give a room a warm, rustic feel.
terms.simple_definition: A ceiling with its wooden or steel beams left on show.

terms.definition: A thick-walled, domed, lockable market hall in Ottoman bazaars where valuable goods such as fine fabrics and jewellery were stored and sold.
terms.simple_definition: A strong, domed Ottoman market hall for valuable goods.

terms.definition: A design approach that strengthens people's connection to nature by bringing daylight, plants, water, natural materials and views of nature into buildings.
terms.simple_definition: Designing spaces with plants, daylight and natural materials to feel closer to nature.

terms.definition: A sticky, waterproof black substance derived from petroleum. It is used to waterproof roofs and foundations and as the binder in asphalt.
terms.simple_definition: A sticky black material that keeps water out of roofs and foundations.

terms.definition: A thick threaded metal rod used with a nut to clamp steel or timber parts tightly together.
terms.simple_definition: A thick screw used with a nut to hold parts together.

terms.definition: A support, often carved timber or stone, that projects diagonally from a wall to hold up eaves, bay windows or shelves; in traditional Turkish houses it is called "eli böğründe".
terms.simple_definition: A support sticking out from a wall that holds up a roof edge, bay or shelf.

terms.definition: A building façade whose outer surface is built or clad in exposed brick. It is durable, low-maintenance and gives a warm, classic look.
terms.simple_definition: The outside of a building finished in visible brick.

terms.definition: An architectural movement popular from the 1950s to the 1970s, known for raw unpainted concrete, rough textures and massive, heavy forms.
terms.simple_definition: A style using bare grey concrete and big, chunky shapes.

terms.definition: A permanent structure with walls and a roof in which people live, work or store things, such as a house, school or office.
terms.simple_definition: Any structure with walls and a roof that people can go inside.

terms.definition: An appliance such as an oven, hob or dishwasher that is fitted into kitchen cabinets or a wall rather than standing on its own.
terms.simple_definition: A kitchen appliance fitted inside the cupboards.

terms.definition: A thick stone or brick support built against the outside of a tall wall to stop it from leaning outward or toppling. It is common on churches and castle walls.
terms.simple_definition: A thick support leaning against a wall from outside so it does not fall over.

terms.definition: An open, patterned weave made from thin strips of rattan, used on chair seats, chair backs and cabinet doors.
terms.simple_definition: The see-through woven rattan pattern found on chairs.

terms.definition: A structural element fixed at only one end to a wall or column, with the other end projecting freely with no support. Balconies and roof overhangs are often cantilevers.
terms.simple_definition: Something that sticks out from a wall with nothing holding up its far end.

terms.definition: A tradesperson who builds timber roofs, concrete formwork, scaffolding and other structural woodwork on a building site, as opposed to a cabinetmaker who makes furniture.
terms.simple_definition: A builder who makes the wooden parts of a building, such as the roof frame.

terms.definition: The craft of creating patterns, figures or decoration by cutting away material such as wood, stone or marble with chisels and similar tools. It is common on traditional doors, ceilings and furniture.
terms.simple_definition: The craft of cutting patterns into wood or stone with tools.

terms.definition: An electric fan hung from the ceiling whose large blades turn to move the air in a room and make it feel cooler. Many models also include a light.
terms.simple_definition: A fan fixed to the ceiling that spins to cool the room.

terms.definition: A grey powder made by firing limestone and clay at high temperature and grinding them. It hardens when mixed with water and is the binder in concrete and mortar.
terms.simple_definition: The grey powder that hardens with water and glues concrete together.

terms.definition: Cutting a sharp corner of a material at an angle to make a small flat bevel. It is done on wood, stone, concrete and furniture edges for safety and appearance.
terms.simple_definition: Cutting off a sharp corner at an angle to soften it.

terms.definition: A classic English sofa with rolled arms the same height as its back and deep-buttoned (tufted) upholstery, usually in leather.
terms.simple_definition: A classic buttoned leather sofa with rolled arms.

terms.definition: All the spaces people use to move around a building, such as corridors, halls, stairs and lifts. Good circulation makes getting from place to place short and easy.
terms.simple_definition: The routes you use to move between rooms in a building.

terms.definition: The water tank behind a toilet or hidden inside the wall that empties to flush the toilet. Ones hidden in the wall are called concealed cisterns.
terms.simple_definition: The water tank that empties when you flush the toilet.

terms.definition: In a zoning plan, an area of land bounded by streets on all sides and divided into one or more plots.
terms.simple_definition: A piece of land surrounded by streets on all sides.

terms.definition: An outer layer of stone, composite panels, ceramic, timber or metal fixed over a building's external walls. It protects the structure from the weather and defines how the building looks.
terms.simple_definition: The protective and decorative outer skin on a building's walls.

terms.definition: Architecture based on the column orders, symmetry, pediments and balanced proportions of ancient Greek and Roman buildings, revived many times in later centuries.
terms.simple_definition: The symmetrical, column-based style of ancient Greece and Rome.

terms.definition: A fine-grained earth that can be shaped when wet and hardens when dried or fired. It is the main raw material of bricks, roof tiles, ceramics and adobe.
terms.simple_definition: Mouldable earth used to make bricks and roof tiles.

terms.definition: A small Ottoman building, usually in a mosque courtyard, where prayer times were calculated and the town's clocks were set. The official who worked there was called the muvakkit.
terms.simple_definition: A small old building where the exact time and prayer times were worked out.

terms.definition: A low table placed in front of or between sofas and armchairs, used for drinks, books or decorative objects.
terms.simple_definition: The low table in front of the sofa in a living room.

terms.definition: A ceiling made of a grid of sunken square, rectangular or octagonal panels. It is decorative and also lightens the ceiling.
terms.simple_definition: A ceiling covered in a grid of sunken square panels.

terms.definition: A group of matching colors chosen to be used together in a room or project. It keeps the colors of walls, furniture, fabrics and accessories consistent.
terms.simple_definition: A set of colors chosen to look good together in a room.

terms.definition: A vertical structural member that collects the load of the floors and beams above and carries it down to the foundation. Usually concrete or steel, it must never be cut or drilled carelessly.
terms.simple_definition: An upright support that holds up the building and carries its weight to the ground.

terms.definition: The state in which temperature, humidity, air quality, light and sound levels in a space make people feel at ease. Good design balances these conditions.
terms.simple_definition: When a room's temperature, light and sound make you feel at ease.

terms.definition: A building material made by mixing cement, water, sand and gravel; it is poured into moulds and hardens into a stone-like mass.
terms.simple_definition: A mix of cement, sand, gravel and water that sets as hard as stone.

terms.definition: A movement born in 1920s Soviet Russia which held that art and architecture should serve society, featuring industrial materials such as steel, glass and concrete and sharp geometric forms.
terms.simple_definition: A 1920s Russian style using industrial materials and bold geometric shapes.

terms.definition: In design, placing clearly different elements side by side, in colour, light, texture, material or shape, to create interest and emphasis.
terms.simple_definition: Putting opposites together, like light and dark or rough and smooth.

terms.definition: A sloped stone, concrete or metal cap laid on top of a garden wall, parapet or balustrade wall to stop rainwater soaking into the wall.
terms.simple_definition: A sloped cap on top of a wall that sheds rain.

terms.definition: Laying stones, bricks, tiles or timbers so that each course slightly overhangs or overlaps the one below. Corbelled domes and arches are built this way without true arches.
terms.simple_definition: Stacking pieces so each layer sticks out a little further than the one below.

terms.definition: An L-shaped metal profile bent at a right angle. It is used to join two parts at a corner, support shelves, or protect wall and step edges from knocks.
terms.simple_definition: An L-shaped metal strip used to join or protect corners.

terms.definition: A metal, wooden or plastic track or rod fixed to the ceiling or top of a wall from which curtains hang. In Turkish the same word (korniş) also means a projecting cornice moulding.
terms.simple_definition: The rail or rod that curtains hang from.

terms.definition: A long, narrow passage in a building that connects rooms to each other.
terms.simple_definition: A long, narrow passage between rooms.

terms.definition: The flat, durable work surface on top of kitchen base cabinets, used for preparing food. It is made from materials such as granite, quartz, marble or laminate.
terms.simple_definition: The flat, hard surface in a kitchen where you prepare food.

terms.definition: Indirect lighting hidden in a recess of a ceiling, wall or furniture edge so the light source is not seen. It bounces light off surfaces for a soft, glare-free glow.
terms.simple_definition: Lights tucked out of sight in a ceiling or wall recess for a soft glow.

terms.definition: A decorative plaster or polyurethane moulding fitted where a wall meets the ceiling. It hides the joint and gives the room a classic finish.
terms.simple_definition: A decorative strip along the line where wall meets ceiling.

terms.definition: A vault formed where two barrel vaults cross at right angles. It gathers the load onto four corner supports, leaving the walls free for large openings.
terms.simple_definition: A ceiling made where two tunnel-shaped vaults cross each other.

terms.definition: A single straight reinforcing bar with hooked ends that ties opposite main bars and stirrups together in concrete columns and beams. It stops the bars bursting outwards in an earthquake.
terms.simple_definition: A short hooked steel bar that ties the rebar together inside a column.

terms.definition: The edge of a roof that overhangs the outer walls; "çelen" is a regional Anatolian word for it. It throws rainwater clear of the walls and shades the façade.
terms.simple_definition: The part of a roof that sticks out past the walls.

terms.definition: A vaulted underground room beneath a church, used as a burial chamber, a place for relics or a small chapel.
terms.simple_definition: An underground stone room beneath a church.

terms.definition: A long, vaulted, partly underground corridor in ancient Roman buildings, used as a cool storeroom, a passage or the supporting base for the structure above.
terms.simple_definition: A covered, partly underground Roman corridor.

terms.definition: An enclosed, windowed projection from the upper floor of a traditional Turkish house over the street. It adds space and light and gives views in three directions.
terms.simple_definition: A windowed room-bulge jutting out over the street from an upper floor.

terms.definition: A non-load-bearing façade system of aluminium-framed glass or panels hung on the outside of a building's structural frame. The big glass skins of skyscrapers are curtain walls.
terms.simple_definition: A thin, usually glass outer skin hung on a building's frame.

terms.definition: A large barrier built across a river to hold back water for drinking supply, irrigation or electricity generation.
terms.simple_definition: A huge wall built across a river to store water.

terms.definition: An architectural movement of the 1980s that deliberately breaks traditional order and symmetry with tilted, fragmented, seemingly unstable forms; Frank Gehry and Zaha Hadid are well-known figures.
terms.simple_definition: A style that makes buildings look deliberately tilted, broken up and off-balance.

terms.definition: Making a space more attractive, practical and personal through the choice of colours, furniture, lighting, textiles and accessories.
terms.simple_definition: Making a room look nice with colours, furniture and objects.

terms.definition: A steel bar with raised ridges on its surface, placed inside concrete in reinforced concrete buildings. The ridges help the steel grip the concrete firmly.
terms.simple_definition: The bumpy steel bars put inside concrete to make it stronger.

terms.definition: A house that stands alone on its own plot and shares no walls with any other building. It usually has its own garden and entrance.
terms.simple_definition: A house that stands on its own, not attached to any other house.

terms.definition: A low seating platform running along the walls of a room in traditional Turkish houses, covered with cushions and pillows. It is usually placed beneath the windows.
terms.simple_definition: A long, low cushioned seat along the walls of an old Turkish house.

terms.definition: A roof or ceiling shaped like half a sphere, usually rising from a circular base. It can cover large spaces without inner supports.
terms.simple_definition: A rounded roof shaped like half a ball.

terms.definition: Leading rainwater and groundwater away from a building's foundations and surroundings using pipes, gravel beds and slopes. It keeps basements and foundations dry.
terms.simple_definition: A system that carries water away from a building.

terms.definition: A scaled technical drawing showing a building's plans, sections, elevations and details; builders read from these drawings what to build and how.
terms.simple_definition: A measured drawing that shows exactly how to build something.

terms.definition: The ability of a building material or component to keep doing its job for a long time without deteriorating from moisture, sun, wear, frost and age.
terms.simple_definition: How long a material lasts before it wears out.

terms.definition: The official, mandatory technical rules for designing and building earthquake-resistant buildings; in Turkey the current version is the 2018 Turkish Building Earthquake Code.
terms.simple_definition: The legal rules that make buildings safe in earthquakes.

terms.definition: Any of the parts that make up a building, such as a wall, column, beam, floor slab, stair, roof, door or window.
terms.simple_definition: Any part of a building, like a wall, column or staircase.

terms.definition: The height or depth of a point, in metres, measured from a chosen reference level such as sea level or the building's entrance floor (±0.00).
terms.simple_definition: A number showing how high or low a point is.

terms.definition: A mechanical system in which a car moving up and down a shaft carries people and goods between floors.
terms.simple_definition: A moving cabin that carries people between floors.

terms.definition: An early-19th-century architecture and furniture style from Napoleonic France, using ancient Roman and Egyptian motifs, laurel wreaths and grand ornament; it also spread in the Ottoman Empire.
terms.simple_definition: A grand, palace-like decorative style from Napoleon's time.

terms.definition: A private bathroom opening directly off the main bedroom and used only by its occupants.
terms.simple_definition: A private bathroom you enter from the bedroom.

terms.definition: Keeping the energy a building needs for heating, cooling, lighting and hot water to a minimum through good insulation, smart orientation and efficient systems.
terms.simple_definition: A building using less energy for the same comfort.

terms.definition: The door through which you enter a building or space, together with the welcoming area in front of it. It is a key part of design because it sets the first impression.
terms.simple_definition: The doorway and area where you enter a building.

terms.definition: The first indoor space you enter in a house or flat, leading on to the other rooms; shoe cabinets and coat stands are usually placed here.
terms.simple_definition: The small area just inside the front door.

terms.definition: Arranging the open areas around a building, including footpaths, parking, garden walls, planting and outdoor lighting.
terms.simple_definition: Designing the paths, gardens and parking around a building.

terms.definition: A tough resin that hardens when two components are mixed. It is used as a strong adhesive and as a seamless, glossy floor coating in garages, factories and homes.
terms.simple_definition: A very strong resin used as glue and as a shiny, seamless floor.

terms.definition: Designing furniture, spaces and equipment to fit the size and movements of the human body so that they are comfortable, safe and not tiring to use.
terms.simple_definition: Designing things to fit the human body comfortably.

terms.definition: An open, multi-tiered shelving unit without doors for displaying ornaments, books or small items; it can stand on the floor or hang on the wall.
terms.simple_definition: An open set of shelves without doors.

terms.definition: A gap left between parts of a building so they can move independently as temperatures change, the ground settles or an earthquake strikes. It prevents cracking and damage.
terms.simple_definition: A gap that lets parts of a building move without cracking.

terms.definition: Concrete left bare after the formwork is removed, without plaster or paint, showing the texture of the mould on its surface. It is used decoratively in modern and industrial spaces.
terms.simple_definition: Bare grey concrete left unplastered and unpainted.

terms.definition: Any of the outer faces of a building, especially the main front, whose windows, entrance and materials give the building its character.
terms.simple_definition: The outside face of a building.

terms.definition: The core design idea that decides how rooms, routes and functions are arranged in relation to each other and how they are experienced as you move through a building.
terms.simple_definition: The main idea of how rooms and spaces fit together.

terms.definition: A staircase built so people can leave a building safely in an emergency such as a fire, usually on the outside wall or in a protected enclosed shaft.
terms.simple_definition: The stairs used to get out of a building safely during a fire.

terms.definition: In plumbing, the taps, mixers and shower heads that turn water on and off and direct it. In Turkish the same word (armatür) is also used for a light fitting.
terms.simple_definition: The taps and mixers on sinks and showers.

terms.definition: A lamp that stands on the floor on a tall stand. It is used in living areas as a reading light or to add soft light to a room.
terms.simple_definition: A tall lamp that stands on the floor.

terms.definition: Usually square or rectangular slabs of ceramic, porcelain or stone used to cover floors. Because they are durable and easy to clean, they are common in kitchens, bathrooms and halls.
terms.simple_definition: Ceramic or stone pieces laid to cover a floor.

terms.definition: The horizontal structural plate, usually reinforced concrete, that separates storeys and that you walk on; the word is also used for the floor finish laid on top.
terms.simple_definition: The flat structural floor that separates one storey from the next.

terms.definition: Shallow vertical channels carved along the length of a column or surface. Common on ancient Greek columns, they make the column look taller and slimmer.
terms.simple_definition: The long grooves carved down the side of a column.

terms.definition: A type of buttress that reaches in an arch from the upper part of a tall wall to a separate stone pier outside. On Gothic cathedrals it carries the outward push of the roof, allowing large windows.
terms.simple_definition: A stone arm that bridges out from a wall to a pillar outside to hold the wall up.

terms.definition: Supplying fresh air to a space and extracting stale air using fans and ducts instead of relying on open windows. Common in bathrooms, kitchens and car parks.
terms.simple_definition: Using fans to bring in fresh air and remove stale air.

terms.definition: A temporary timber, metal or plastic mould into which fresh concrete is poured and which holds its shape until it hardens; it is removed once the concrete is strong enough.
terms.simple_definition: The temporary mould that shapes concrete until it sets.

terms.definition: A railing fixed across a floor-to-ceiling window or door without a projecting platform, so there is no floor to step out onto.
terms.simple_definition: A railing across a tall window with no floor to stand on.

terms.definition: A wall or ceiling painting made with water-based pigments on fresh, wet lime plaster. As the plaster dries the paint becomes part of the wall, so it lasts for centuries.
terms.simple_definition: A painting made on wet plaster so it becomes part of the wall.

terms.definition: A horizontal band with carved or painted decoration running along the upper part of a wall, or above the architrave in classical buildings.
terms.simple_definition: A decorated band running along the top of a wall.

terms.definition: What a space or building is used for, and how well it meets the needs of that use; for example, a kitchen's functions of cooking, storage and cleaning.
terms.simple_definition: What a room or building is used for.

terms.definition: The maximum height, number of storeys and outer limits that zoning rules allow for a building on a plot; the imaginary envelope the building must fit inside.
terms.simple_definition: The rule for how tall and big a building is allowed to be.

terms.definition: A wall built from galvanised wire cages filled with stones and stacked together. Used for retaining walls, slope protection and landscaping; because water drains through it, it is very stable.
terms.simple_definition: A wall made of wire cages filled with stones.

terms.definition: A roof with two sloping sides meeting at a ridge at the top, leaving a triangular wall (gable) at each end.
terms.simple_definition: The classic triangle-shaped roof that slopes down on two sides.

terms.definition: A space whose ceiling is left open through two or more storeys, so the lower floor can be seen from above. The word also means a room or building for showing art.
terms.simple_definition: A double-height open space you can look down into from the floor above.

terms.definition: A low or medium-height wall marking the edge of a plot or garden and providing privacy and security; its height is usually limited by local building rules.
terms.simple_definition: The wall around a garden or plot.

terms.definition: A spout projecting from a building that throws rainwater from the roof away from the walls. On Gothic buildings it is often carved as an animal or monster.
terms.simple_definition: A spout, often carved like a monster, that throws roof rainwater away from the walls.

terms.definition: A small, roofed garden pavilion with open sides, often hexagonal or octagonal, built for sitting and relaxing outdoors.
terms.simple_definition: A little open-sided, roofed garden shelter for sitting.

terms.definition: A hollow, thick-glass block shaped like a brick. It is used for walls and partitions that let light through while keeping privacy.
terms.simple_definition: A brick made of thick glass that lets light in but blurs the view.

terms.definition: A building façade made entirely or mostly of glass. It lets in plenty of daylight but needs special glazing to control heat and sun.
terms.simple_definition: A building face made almost entirely of glass.

terms.definition: A framed or frameless glass wall that divides a space without blocking light. Common in offices and open-plan homes.
terms.simple_definition: A see-through glass wall that splits one room into two.

terms.definition: A European style from the 12th to 16th centuries, known for pointed arches, ribbed vaults, flying buttresses, soaring ceilings and large stained-glass windows.
terms.simple_definition: The style of tall medieval cathedrals with pointed arches and stained glass.

terms.definition: A building designed to use energy and water efficiently, built with eco-friendly materials and to cause as little harm to nature as possible. It can be certified by schemes such as LEED or BREEAM.
terms.simple_definition: A building that uses little energy and is kind to the environment.

terms.definition: A building face planted with climbing plants or with modular systems holding soil or a growing medium. It cools the building, cleans the air and reduces noise.
terms.simple_definition: A building wall covered in living plants.

terms.definition: Increasing an existing building's resistance to earthquakes and loads, for example by jacketing columns, adding shear walls or wrapping members with steel or carbon fibre.
terms.simple_definition: Making an existing building stronger against earthquakes.

terms.definition: A white powder made by heating and grinding gypsum rock. Mixed with water it forms a paste that sets quickly; it is used for interior wall plaster, ceilings and decorative mouldings.
terms.simple_definition: A white powder used to make walls smooth and flat.

terms.definition: Concrete made much lighter than normal by adding pumice, expanded clay or air bubbles. It insulates well; aerated concrete blocks are one type.
terms.simple_definition: Concrete filled with tiny air pockets so it weighs much less.

terms.definition: A circulation space in a home or building onto which the room doors open and which links the rooms together.
terms.simple_definition: The space in a home that connects all the rooms.

terms.definition: A traditional domed Turkish bathhouse with changing, warm and hot rooms where people bathe in steam. It is heated by a furnace that sends hot air through spaces under the floor.
terms.simple_definition: A traditional domed Turkish steam bath.

terms.definition: A multi-storey building with a central courtyard in Seljuk and Ottoman towns where merchants stayed, stored goods and traded.
terms.simple_definition: An old courtyard building in town where merchants stayed and traded.

terms.definition: The horizontal rail at the top of a stair or balcony railing that you hold for support.
terms.simple_definition: The rail you hold onto when going up the stairs.

terms.definition: The private family quarters of a traditional Turkish house or palace, closed to male visitors and separate from the selamlık where guests were received.
terms.simple_definition: The private family part of an old Ottoman house or palace.

terms.definition: A scaled map showing the current state of a site, including its buildings, roads, trees and contour lines. It is the base for design and zoning work.
terms.simple_definition: A measured map showing what is on a site today.

terms.definition: Ready-made reinforcement of steel wires welded into a square or rectangular grid. It is laid in floor slabs, screeds and concrete walls to prevent cracking.
terms.simple_definition: A grid of welded steel wire placed inside concrete.

terms.definition: Removing stale, humid air from a space and replacing it with fresh outdoor air, either naturally through windows or mechanically with fans and ducts.
terms.simple_definition: Letting fresh air in and stale air out of a room.

terms.definition: A waterproofed concrete or prefabricated water basin built for swimming, relaxation or decoration; it needs pumps and filters to keep the water clean and circulating.
terms.simple_definition: A built water basin for swimming or decoration.

terms.definition: Buildings such as fountains, water kiosks, bridges and soup kitchens that were commissioned as acts of charity in the Ottoman era and offered free to the public.
terms.simple_definition: Fountains, bridges and similar buildings donated for public use in Ottoman times.

terms.definition: A small walled or railed graveyard next to an Ottoman mosque, tomb or dervish lodge.
terms.simple_definition: A small enclosed graveyard beside an old mosque.

terms.definition: Materials and methods used in walls, roofs, floors and windows to slow down heat passing in or out of a building. It lowers heating and cooling costs.
terms.simple_definition: A layer that keeps a home warm in winter and cool in summer.

terms.definition: A long, narrow excavation dug in the ground for foundations, pipes or cables, or to collect water.
terms.simple_definition: A long, narrow ditch dug for pipes or foundations.

terms.definition: The whole of the old buildings, streets and squares that reflect the history of a city or neighborhood, together with the character they create. It is the main focus of conservation and restoration work.
terms.simple_definition: The old buildings and streets that give a city its historic character.

terms.definition: Arranging spaces or elements by importance through size, position and emphasis; for example, making the main hall larger and more central than other rooms.
terms.simple_definition: Making the most important spaces stand out by size or position.

terms.definition: A reinforced concrete floor in which the spaces between narrow ribs are filled with lightweight blocks (pumice, polystyrene or clay). It leaves a flat ceiling and makes the floor lighter.
terms.simple_definition: A concrete floor with light blocks inside it to save weight.

terms.definition: An approach to building that spreads out horizontally with low-rise buildings instead of going tall. It aims for neighborhoods that feel human-scaled and closely connected to the street.
terms.simple_definition: Building low, spread-out buildings instead of tall towers.

terms.definition: The general name for buildings made for people to live in permanently, such as houses, flats and villas; zoning plans mark residential areas for this use.
terms.simple_definition: Homes where people live, such as houses and flats.

terms.definition: A small single room, usually opening onto a courtyard, where students or dervishes lived in a madrasa, lodge or monastery.
terms.simple_definition: A small room where a student or monk lived in an old school or monastery.

terms.definition: The face of a building that looks onto an inner courtyard, light well or rear garden rather than the street.
terms.simple_definition: The side of a building facing its courtyard, not the street.

terms.definition: A trained professional who designs the inside of buildings, including layout, materials, lighting, furniture and details, so that spaces are practical, safe and attractive.
terms.simple_definition: A professional who designs the inside of buildings.

terms.definition: The official process of dividing one registered plot of land into two or more separate plots in line with zoning rules.
terms.simple_definition: Officially splitting one plot of land into several.

terms.definition: The set of plans and rules that decide what kind and size of building can be built on each piece of land in a city, set out in zoning plans and regulations.
terms.simple_definition: The official rules on what can be built where, and how big.

terms.definition: A building within an Ottoman mosque complex where free meals were served to the poor, students and travellers.
terms.simple_definition: An Ottoman kitchen that gave free food to people in need.

terms.definition: A plant grown in a pot indoors that tolerates low light and room temperature. Interior designers use it to bring life into a space and freshen the air.
terms.simple_definition: A potted plant kept inside the home.

terms.definition: An interior style inspired by old factories and warehouses, combining exposed brick, raw concrete, visible metal pipes, steel and wood.
terms.simple_definition: A decor style that looks like a converted factory, with brick, concrete and metal.

terms.definition: All the roads and the water, sewerage, electricity, gas and telecom networks that a settlement needs in order to function.
terms.simple_definition: The roads, pipes and cables that serve buildings.

terms.definition: The process of building a structure according to its design, from excavation to handover; also the site where this work takes place.
terms.simple_definition: The work of building something.

terms.definition: A carved stone or marble panel set over the door or on the walls of a historic building, recording when and by whom it was built.
terms.simple_definition: A carved stone sign on an old building saying when and by whom it was built.

terms.definition: The inside of a building enclosed by walls, floors and ceilings, including rooms, halls and other enclosed areas.
terms.simple_definition: All the rooms and areas inside a building.

terms.definition: The certificate issued by the municipality once a finished building is confirmed to match its approved plans and regulations, allowing people to move in.
terms.simple_definition: The official permission to start living in a new building.

terms.definition: The architectural tradition of the Islamic world, seen in mosques, madrasas and tombs, featuring domes, minarets, courtyards, prayer niches and geometric or floral ornament.
terms.simple_definition: The architecture of mosques and madrasas, with domes, minarets and geometric patterns.

terms.definition: A freestanding counter unit in the middle of a kitchen, reachable from all sides, often containing a hob, sink or breakfast bar.
terms.simple_definition: A counter in the middle of the kitchen that you can walk around.

terms.definition: A usually vaulted hall walled on three sides and completely open on the fourth to a courtyard or central hall. Common in Seljuk and Ottoman madrasas, inns and houses.
terms.simple_definition: A room with three walls, fully open on one side to a courtyard.

terms.definition: A regular system of lines crossing at right angles on which a building's columns and walls are placed; in urban planning, a layout where streets cross like a chessboard.
terms.simple_definition: A chessboard-like pattern of lines for placing columns or streets.

terms.definition: A bathtub or small pool with jets that push out water and air for a massage effect. Used in bathroom and spa design; it needs plumbing and electrical connections.
terms.simple_definition: A bathtub with jets that give a water massage.

terms.definition: A thin recessed line deliberately left where two surfaces of plaster, plasterboard, timber or cladding meet. It hides cracks and gives a neat, modern look.
terms.simple_definition: A thin recessed line left on a wall or ceiling for a clean look.

terms.definition: The gap between tiles, stones or bricks, and the grout or mortar that fills it.
terms.simple_definition: The filled lines between tiles or bricks.

terms.definition: A covered plastic box, usually set into a wall, where electrical cables are joined or branched.
terms.simple_definition: A small box in the wall where electrical wires are connected.

terms.definition: A screen of thin wooden slats joined in a criss-cross pattern, fitted over windows in traditional Ottoman houses so people inside could see out without being seen.
terms.simple_definition: A wooden lattice over old windows that lets you see out but not in.

terms.definition: Construction made by laying units such as stone, brick or concrete blocks in mortar, and the buildings made this way; in masonry buildings the walls carry the load.
terms.simple_definition: Building with stone or bricks stacked and joined with mortar.

terms.definition: The bottom part on which a column, statue or monument stands, raising it above the ground.
terms.simple_definition: The block a column or statue stands on.

terms.definition: The paved strip alongside a road, slightly raised above the carriageway, reserved for pedestrians.
terms.simple_definition: The raised path beside a road where people walk.

terms.definition: Traditional decoration painted by brush on plaster or timber surfaces, with floral and geometric motifs, seen on mosque domes, ceilings and pavilions.
terms.simple_definition: Traditional patterns hand-painted on ceilings and walls.

terms.definition: The moving part of a door or window that is hinged to the frame and opens and closes.
terms.simple_definition: The part of a door or window that swings open.

terms.definition: A building component consisting of a frame and an opening leaf that lets people enter and leave a space.
terms.simple_definition: The part that opens and closes so you can go in and out of a room.

terms.definition: The layer of material that gives floors, walls or ceilings their final look and protects them, such as parquet, ceramic tile, stone, timber or wallpaper.
terms.simple_definition: The top layer covering a floor or wall, like tiles or wood.

terms.definition: A covered pit or structure dug into the ground where winter snow was packed and stored for use in summer before refrigerators existed.
terms.simple_definition: An old underground pit used to store winter snow for summer.

terms.definition: A usually square slab of ceramic, marble or cement used to cover floors and walls; the patterned cement tiles of old houses are a well-known example.
terms.simple_definition: A square tile laid on floors.

terms.definition: The fixed frame set into a wall opening, to which the door or window leaf is hinged.
terms.simple_definition: The fixed frame that a door or window hangs in.

terms.definition: A small palace or pavilion, usually set in a garden or by the water, used by Ottoman sultans and dignitaries for relaxation.
terms.simple_definition: A small Ottoman palace for resting, often in a garden.

terms.definition: A natural stone that splits easily into thin, flat plates. It is traditionally used for roofing, flooring and wall cladding.
terms.simple_definition: A stone that splits into thin flat sheets, used on roofs and floors.

terms.definition: A plant room, usually in the basement, housing the boiler, pumps and pipework that supply a building's heating and hot water.
terms.simple_definition: The room where a building's heating boiler is kept.

terms.definition: A security cover of metal or aluminium slats fitted over a shopfront, garage or window that rolls up to open.
terms.simple_definition: A metal cover that rolls down over a shop window or door.

terms.definition: An unfired brick made by pouring a mix of clay, water and straw into moulds and drying it in the sun. Used in Anatolia for thousands of years, it keeps indoor temperatures steady.
terms.simple_definition: A brick made of mud and straw dried in the sun.

terms.definition: A large, thick-walled courtyard building on Seljuk and Ottoman trade routes where caravans and travellers could stay safely overnight.
terms.simple_definition: A big walled roadside inn for travelling merchants and their animals.

terms.definition: The wedge-shaped stone placed last at the very top of a stone arch. It locks the other stones together and keeps the arch standing.
terms.simple_definition: The top stone of an arch that holds all the others in place.

terms.definition: A traditional Anatolian flat-woven rug with no pile and geometric patterns, laid on floors or hung on walls in interiors.
terms.simple_definition: A thin, flat-woven rug with geometric patterns.

terms.definition: A Christian place of worship, usually with a long central nave, an altar area (apse) and a bell tower.
terms.simple_definition: A building where Christians worship.

terms.definition: Concrete paving blocks shaped so their sides lock into each other. Laid without mortar, they are used for sidewalks, car parks and garden paths.
terms.simple_definition: Concrete paving stones that fit together like a puzzle.

terms.definition: The direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face in prayer. In a mosque the prayer niche (mihrab) is set in the wall facing this direction, which shapes the whole layout.
terms.simple_definition: The direction of Mecca that a mosque is built to face.

terms.definition: The legally defined line marking how far water reaches along seas, lakes and rivers. Permanent buildings are not allowed within a set distance of this line.
terms.simple_definition: The official waterfront line that limits how close you can build.

terms.definition: An Ottoman group of buildings centred on a mosque, including a madrasa, soup kitchen, bath, hospital and tomb.
terms.simple_definition: A group of buildings around a mosque, such as a school, kitchen and bath.

terms.definition: A staircase that turns 90 degrees at a landing, forming the shape of the letter L. It saves space because it can fit into a corner.
terms.simple_definition: A staircase that turns a corner halfway, like the letter L.

terms.definition: An electrical device made of a bulb and the body that holds it, used to light a space. It can be ceiling, wall, table or floor mounted and strongly shapes the mood of a room.
terms.simple_definition: An electric light that brightens a room.

terms.definition: A fabric, paper, metal or glass cover that softens a lamp's light and directs it downwards or to one side; in Turkish the word also means a table or floor lamp with such a shade.
terms.simple_definition: The hat-like cover that softens a lamp's light.

terms.definition: The flat area at the top, bottom or between two flights of a staircase. It lets the stairs change direction and gives people a place to pause.
terms.simple_definition: The flat part at the top of or in the middle of a staircase.

terms.definition: Planning and shaping the outdoor space around a building with plants, trees, paths, water features and seating areas. It applies at every scale, from a garden to a city park.
terms.simple_definition: Designing the garden and outdoor space around a building.

terms.definition: A small tower-like structure with windows all around, set on top of a dome or roof to let light and air in from above.
terms.simple_definition: A little windowed tower on top of a dome.

terms.definition: A traditional technique in which thin timber strips are nailed in rows across a timber-framed wall or ceiling and then covered with lime or gypsum plaster; common in old Turkish houses.
terms.simple_definition: An old way of making walls by plastering over thin wooden strips.

terms.definition: Unreinforced concrete with little cement, poured as a thin layer at the bottom of a foundation pit to give a flat, clean base for the real foundation.
terms.simple_definition: A thin, simple concrete layer poured to level the ground under a foundation.

terms.definition: Planning daylight and artificial light so that a space gets the right amount and quality of light for its use, typically in layers of general, task and accent lighting.
terms.simple_definition: Planning how a space is lit so it has the right light.

terms.definition: The complete lighting unit, such as a chandelier, spotlight or wall light, that holds the bulb or LED, spreads the light and connects to the power supply.
terms.simple_definition: The lamp body that a bulb fits into, like a ceiling light or spotlight.

terms.definition: A walled, below-ground space dug in front of basement windows so that daylight and fresh air can reach the basement.
terms.simple_definition: A pit dug in front of a basement window so it gets light.

terms.definition: A horizontal beam placed over a door or window opening to carry the weight of the wall above. It can be made of reinforced concrete, steel, stone or timber.
terms.simple_definition: The horizontal piece above a door or window that holds up the wall.

terms.definition: The general name for the parts of a home where daily life happens, such as the living room, kitchen and dining area. Bedrooms and bathrooms are usually counted separately.
terms.simple_definition: The rooms where you spend most of your day, like the living room and kitchen.

terms.definition: High-priced homes, usually in a prime location, that stand out for quality materials, generous space, bespoke design and extras such as a pool, security or a gym.
terms.simple_definition: An expensive, spacious home with high-quality materials and many extras.

terms.definition: A traditional higher-education building in the Islamic world, common in the Ottoman Empire. It usually has student rooms and a lecture hall arranged around a courtyard with a covered colonnade.
terms.simple_definition: An old school building where students studied and lived around a courtyard.

terms.definition: A kitchen or bathroom countertop made of marble. Its natural veining looks elegant, but because marble is porous it needs regular care against acids and stains.
terms.simple_definition: A kitchen or bathroom counter made of marble stone.

terms.definition: The largest, most richly decorated room with the best view in a traditional Turkish house, usually used to receive guests.
terms.simple_definition: The biggest and finest room of an old Turkish house, used for guests.

terms.definition: The general name for substances such as concrete, brick, stone, timber, steel and glass used to build and finish a building. The choice of material shapes a building's durability, cost and appearance.
terms.simple_definition: The stuff used to make buildings, like brick, concrete and wood.

terms.definition: A thin, flexible waterproofing sheet laid on roofs, foundations or wet areas to stop water getting into the building. There are bitumen-based and synthetic (such as PVC or TPO) types.
terms.simple_definition: A thin waterproof sheet laid to keep water out of a building.

terms.definition: An intermediate floor built inside a double-height space, partly open to the floor below. It is common in shops, offices and loft apartments to gain extra space.
terms.simple_definition: A half-floor inside a tall room that looks down on the floor below.

terms.definition: A design approach that removes unnecessary decoration and objects, focusing on simple forms, open space and a few well-chosen materials. It is summed up by the phrase "less is more".
terms.simple_definition: Creating calm, uncluttered spaces with few objects and simple lines.

terms.definition: In joinery, the flat or raised board, stone or glass sheet fitted inside the frame of a door or cabinet door.
terms.simple_definition: The flat or raised panel set inside a door's frame.

terms.definition: An architectural movement from the early 20th century that rejected ornament and put function first. It uses concrete, steel and glass in simple geometric forms, with large windows and open plans.
terms.simple_definition: A 20th-century style of plain, undecorated buildings using lots of glass and steel.

terms.definition: A design system built by combining units of standard sizes that can be added or removed as needed. Modular kitchen cabinets and furniture are the best-known examples.
terms.simple_definition: A design made of same-size pieces that can be combined and rearranged.

terms.definition: A building made in a factory as rooms or sections, transported to the site and assembled there. It is completed much faster than a traditionally built building.
terms.simple_definition: A building made in a factory in pieces and quickly put together on site.

terms.definition: A statue, building or symbolic structure built to commemorate an important person or event and to remind future generations of it.
terms.simple_definition: A structure built to remember an important person or event.

terms.definition: A board that brings together photos, colors, fabrics and material samples to show the intended feel and style of a project. It helps the designer and client share the same vision.
terms.simple_definition: A board of pictures and color samples that shows how a space will look.

terms.definition: A paste of sand, a binder (cement or lime) and water used to bond bricks and stones together or to plaster walls.
terms.simple_definition: The paste used to stick bricks together.

terms.definition: A Muslim place of communal prayer, usually with a prayer niche (mihrab), pulpit (minbar), dome, minaret and a courtyard with an ablution fountain.
terms.simple_definition: A building where Muslims pray, usually with a dome and minaret.

terms.definition: A durable wall built from quarried stones, cut or left rough, laid with or without mortar.
terms.simple_definition: A wall built from real stones stacked together.

terms.definition: An architectural style that emerged in the mid-18th century, inspired by ancient Greek and Roman buildings. It features symmetry, columns, triangular pediments and plain but grand facades.
terms.simple_definition: Columned, symmetrical buildings that look like ancient Greek and Roman temples.

terms.definition: A shallow recess set into a wall. It is used to display a statue, vase or ornament, or simply to add depth to the wall.
terms.simple_definition: A small recess in a wall where you can place decorations.

terms.definition: A small cabinet, often with drawers, placed beside the bed to hold a lamp, books and other items.
terms.simple_definition: A small table or cabinet next to the bed.

terms.definition: A round window or opening at the top of a dome or in a wall. The opening in the dome of the Pantheon in Rome is the most famous example.
terms.simple_definition: A round window or hole at the top of a dome or in a wall.

terms.definition: An open-air place for prayer built in Ottoman times outside towns, along roads or in recreation areas. It usually consists of a prayer-niche stone and a stone-paved area.
terms.simple_definition: An outdoor, stone-paved spot made for praying.

terms.definition: A gap left in a wall for a door, window or ventilation. The wall above it is carried by a lintel or an arch.
terms.simple_definition: The hole in a wall where a door or window goes.

terms.definition: Auxiliary structures that belong to a main building but stand apart from it, such as a garage, shed, storeroom or caretaker's house. In deeds and plans they are shown as part of the main property.
terms.simple_definition: Small separate buildings next to a main house, like a garage or shed.

terms.definition: The Ottoman palace art workshop where designs such as book illumination, tile patterns and building ornament were created. Patterns drawn here were applied in mosques and palaces.
terms.simple_definition: An Ottoman workshop where artists drew decorative patterns for buildings.

terms.definition: A door whose frame holds rectangular sections (panels) that are recessed or raised from the surface. It is common in classic and traditional interiors.
terms.simple_definition: A door with framed rectangular sections on its surface.

terms.definition: Long, narrow strips of wood, PVC or metal that slot into each other along their edges to cover a wall or ceiling. It is common in saunas, balcony ceilings and country houses.
terms.simple_definition: Long thin boards that slot together to cover a wall or ceiling.

terms.definition: A small, cool room or cupboard in a home where food, supplies and kitchen items are stored.
terms.simple_definition: A small room for storing food.

terms.definition: A low protective wall along the edge of a roof, terrace, balcony or bridge that prevents falls. On flat roofs it also forms the top edge of the facade.
terms.simple_definition: A low wall along the edge of a roof or balcony that stops people falling.

terms.definition: A piece of land whose boundaries and plot number are fixed in the land registry. The zoning plan decides how much and what kind of building can go on it.
terms.simple_definition: A piece of land with officially marked borders.

terms.definition: Flooring made of wooden or wood-look strips. There are solid, engineered and laminate types, and it can be laid in patterns such as herringbone.
terms.simple_definition: Wooden or wood-look boards that cover a floor.

terms.definition: A non-load-bearing wall built only to divide a space into rooms; it can be made of brick, aerated concrete blocks or plasterboard.
terms.simple_definition: A wall that splits a room in two but doesn't hold up the building.

terms.definition: The triangular wall formed by the roof at the front of a classical building, often decorated with sculpture; also used as an ornament over doors and windows.
terms.simple_definition: The triangle-shaped decoration above a classical building's entrance.

terms.definition: A light fixture that hangs down from the ceiling on a cord, chain or rod. It is often used above dining tables and kitchen islands.
terms.simple_definition: A lamp that hangs down from the ceiling on a cord.

terms.definition: A curved triangular element in the corners of a square room that allows a round dome to sit on top. It can be seen in Hagia Sophia and Ottoman mosques.
terms.simple_definition: The curved triangle in a corner that lets a round dome sit on square walls.

terms.definition: A door that opens by rotating on a pin fitted at its top and bottom instead of on side hinges. It lets very large, heavy doors open easily and is popular for modern entrances.
terms.simple_definition: A door that swings open by turning on a central pin instead of side hinges.

terms.definition: A drawing of a building as if it were sliced horizontally and seen from above. It shows the layout and sizes of rooms, walls, doors and windows.
terms.simple_definition: A map of a building drawn as if seen from above.

terms.definition: A board made by gluing thin layers of wood on top of each other with the grain of each layer at right angles. Being strong and light, it is used in furniture, formwork and cladding.
terms.simple_definition: A strong board made from thin layers of wood glued together.

terms.definition: A platform raised above the ground. In architecture it also means the wide, low base block underneath a tall tower.
terms.simple_definition: A raised flat platform.

terms.definition: A small covered structure with open sides, built in front of an entrance or against a wall. It protects the entrance from rain and sun.
terms.simple_definition: A small roof over the front door that keeps the rain off.

terms.definition: A covered entrance in front of a building, supported by columns. It is often topped by a triangular pediment and is typical of classical buildings.
terms.simple_definition: A grand entrance with a roof held up by columns.

terms.definition: A covered gallery open on one side, formed by a row of columns or piers and the arches they carry along the edge of a courtyard or building. It is common in mosque and madrasa courtyards.
terms.simple_definition: A shaded, roofed walkway with a row of columns along one side.

terms.definition: A vertical member in a timber or steel structure that carries load or holds a frame upright; temporary supports on building sites are also called props.
terms.simple_definition: An upright pole that holds something up.

terms.definition: The first design stage, before the final project, showing the building's overall layout, plans and elevations; it is agreed with the client and authorities at this stage.
terms.simple_definition: The first overall design of a building before the details.

terms.definition: Concrete that is squeezed in advance by tensioning steel cables inside it before or after casting. This lets thinner members span longer distances; it is used in bridges and car parks.
terms.simple_definition: Concrete made stronger by tightly stretched steel cables inside it.

terms.definition: An enclosed or open part of the upper floors that sticks out beyond the main line of a façade. Zoning rules limit how far such projections may extend.
terms.simple_definition: A part of an upper floor that sticks out from the building's face.

terms.definition: A wide pedestrian path designed for walking and strolling, often along a waterfront. In architecture it also describes a walking route through a building that reveals changing views.
terms.simple_definition: A long, wide path made for strolling, such as a seafront walk.

terms.definition: The recording, maintenance, repair and legal protection carried out to keep historic buildings and townscapes alive without losing their original character.
terms.simple_definition: Protecting historic buildings so they survive unspoilt.

terms.definition: A protective barrier of posts and a top rail along the edges of stairs, balconies and terraces that stops people from falling.
terms.simple_definition: The barrier on balconies and stairs that stops you falling.

terms.definition: A sloping surface that links two different levels, in addition to or instead of stairs. It makes access easier for wheelchairs, pushchairs and vehicles.
terms.simple_definition: A sloping path that lets you go up without using steps.

terms.definition: Concrete with steel bars (rebar) set inside it. Concrete resists squeezing and steel resists pulling, so together they form a very strong, earthquake-resistant structure.
terms.simple_definition: Concrete made stronger with steel bars inside.

terms.definition: The ribbed steel bars placed inside reinforced concrete members to make up for concrete's weakness in tension.
terms.simple_definition: The steel bars placed inside concrete.

terms.definition: A sculpture or decoration carved or raised from a flat surface such as a wall, stone or wood. The figures stay attached to the surface rather than standing free.
terms.simple_definition: A picture or pattern that sticks out from a wall surface.

terms.definition: Fixing broken, damaged or worn parts of a building so they can be used again. It covers jobs such as fixing a plumbing fault, a roof leak or crumbling plaster.
terms.simple_definition: Fixing things in a building that are broken or worn out.

terms.definition: Architecture developed in Turkey after the Republic was founded in 1923, covering the First National Style with Ottoman motifs, then plain modernist buildings and the Second National Style.
terms.simple_definition: The building styles that developed after the Turkish Republic was founded.

terms.definition: Repairing the damaged parts of a historic building and returning it to its earlier state while staying true to its original materials and techniques. It is carried out with research and official permits.
terms.simple_definition: Repairing an old historic building so it looks as it originally did.

terms.definition: A vault with stone ribs (slender arches) running along the lines where its curved surfaces meet. In Gothic cathedrals it channels the load to set points, allowing taller, lighter ceilings.
terms.simple_definition: A vaulted ceiling with curved stone ribs showing like a skeleton.

terms.definition: How strongly a building or structural element resists bending and changing shape when forces act on it. It limits how much a building sways in earthquakes and wind.
terms.simple_definition: How well a building resists bending or swaying when pushed.

terms.definition: The vertical face between two treads of a staircase; it sets the height of each step. On a comfortable stair the riser is usually about 15-18 cm.
terms.simple_definition: The upright part between two stair steps.

terms.definition: An 18th-century decorative style from France, lighter and more playful than Baroque. It uses curving lines, shell and plant motifs, pastel colors and plenty of gilding.
terms.simple_definition: A very ornate 18th-century style full of curly decoration and pastel colors.

terms.definition: A medieval architectural style common in Europe from roughly the 10th to 12th centuries, known for thick walls, semicircular arches, small windows and massive towers.
terms.simple_definition: A medieval style of thick-walled churches and castles with round arches.

terms.definition: The covering on top of a building that protects it from rain, snow, sun and wind, made up of a supporting frame, insulation and an outer covering such as tiles.
terms.simple_definition: The top covering of a building that keeps out rain and sun.

terms.definition: The building stage in which the main structure, including foundations, columns, beams, slabs, walls and roof, is built, before plastering, painting and finishes.
terms.simple_definition: Building the bare structure of a house before the finishing work.

terms.definition: A temporary metal or timber platform system put up against a building so workers can safely reach and work at height during construction or repair.
terms.simple_definition: A temporary frame workers stand on to reach high parts of a building.

terms.definition: The ratio between sizes on a drawing or model and the real sizes. For example, on a 1:100 plan, 1 cm represents 1 meter in reality.
terms.simple_definition: How many times smaller a drawing is than the real building.

terms.definition: A technical drawing showing the inside of a building as if it were sliced through vertically, revealing floor heights, stairs and slabs.
terms.simple_definition: A drawing that shows a building as if sliced in half.

terms.definition: A large L-shaped seating unit made of joined sections, designed to fit into the corner of a room.
terms.simple_definition: An L-shaped sofa that fits into a corner.

terms.definition: In a traditional Turkish house, the raised part of a room beyond the entrance area where shoes are not worn; also a raised stone platform for sitting in courtyards or gardens.
terms.simple_definition: A slightly raised area in a room or courtyard used for sitting.

terms.definition: In traditional Ottoman mansions, the outward-facing part of the house where men received guests. The private family section was called the harem.
terms.simple_definition: The part of an old Ottoman house where guests were welcomed.

terms.definition: A pair of houses built side by side as mirror images of each other, sharing one common wall.
terms.simple_definition: Two houses that share one wall in the middle.

terms.definition: The network of pipes and channels that collects wastewater (and sometimes rainwater) from buildings and carries it to a treatment plant.
terms.simple_definition: The underground pipes that carry waste water away from homes.

terms.definition: A fixed or retractable cover fitted above a door, window, balcony or terrace to keep off sun and rain.
terms.simple_definition: A cover over a door or balcony that blocks the sun.

terms.definition: A fountain, often roofed, with taps around it, usually in a mosque courtyard, where worshippers wash before prayer.
terms.simple_definition: A fountain in a mosque courtyard where people wash before praying.

terms.definition: A load-bearing reinforced concrete wall, much longer than a column, built to resist sideways forces such as earthquakes and wind. It greatly reduces how much a building sways.
terms.simple_definition: A strong concrete wall that keeps a building from swaying in earthquakes and wind.

terms.definition: A panel or roller fitted outside a window that can be closed to block sun, light and outside views. Traditional ones are made of slatted wood; modern ones are often rolling aluminum slats.
terms.simple_definition: A cover on the outside of a window that you close to block sun or views.

terms.definition: Usually heavy, decorative curtains hung at either side of a window, framing the sheer curtain.
terms.simple_definition: Thick decorative curtains hung at the sides of a window.

terms.definition: A drawing showing where a building sits on its plot, its distances to neighboring plots and the road, and the layout of entrances, parking and garden. It is a required part of permit drawings.
terms.simple_definition: A drawing that shows where a building sits on its land.

terms.definition: The skeleton of columns, beams and slabs that carries a building's load; the walls are built in between afterwards.
terms.simple_definition: The bones of a building that keep it standing.

terms.definition: A quick, freehand first drawing, not to scale, made to capture and communicate a design idea.
terms.simple_definition: A quick first drawing of an idea.

terms.definition: A strip running along the bottom of a wall where it meets the floor. It covers the joint and protects the wall from knocks by brooms, furniture and feet.
terms.simple_definition: The strip along the bottom of a wall where it meets the floor.

terms.definition: A window or glazed panel set into a roof or ceiling to bring daylight in from above; the word is also used for a light shaft left in the middle of a building.
terms.simple_definition: A window in the roof that lets in sunlight.

terms.definition: A wardrobe or cupboard whose doors slide sideways on tracks instead of swinging open on hinges. It saves space in small rooms because the doors need no clearance in front.
terms.simple_definition: A wardrobe whose doors slide sideways to open.

terms.definition: A home whose lighting, heating, blinds, security and appliances can be controlled remotely by phone, voice commands or automatic routines.
terms.simple_definition: A home whose lights, heating and devices you can control from your phone.

terms.definition: The shared central space in a traditional Turkish house, around which the rooms are arranged and through which they connect. It is where the household gathers and moves around.
terms.simple_definition: The shared central hall of an old Turkish house that all rooms open onto.

terms.definition: The underside of a building element such as roof eaves, a balcony, an arch or a staircase, and the cladding of that surface.
terms.simple_definition: The underside of an overhang, balcony or arch seen from below.

terms.definition: A study of the soil and rock on a plot using drilling and tests before a building is constructed. It is needed to choose the right foundation and assess earthquake risk.
terms.simple_definition: Checking whether the ground is strong enough before building on it.

terms.definition: A panel of photovoltaic cells that converts sunlight directly into electricity, mounted on roofs, façades or open land.
terms.simple_definition: A panel on the roof that makes electricity from sunlight.

terms.definition: An area defined by elements such as walls, floors and ceilings that people occupy and use. It is considered the core material of architecture; a room, courtyard or square are all spaces.
terms.simple_definition: Any place people are in and use, like a room, hall or courtyard.

terms.definition: The horizontal distance a beam, arch or slab covers between its two supports (columns or walls). The longer the span, the stronger the member must be.
terms.simple_definition: The distance between two supports, like two columns.

terms.definition: A staircase whose steps wind upwards around a central post. It takes up little floor space, so it suits tight areas.
terms.simple_definition: A staircase that winds round and round a central pole.

terms.definition: A traditional Turkish house layout in which rooms line both sides of a central hall (sofa) running the full depth of the house.
terms.simple_definition: A house plan with a long central hall and rooms on both sides.

terms.definition: Lighting that directs light at a particular point or object instead of spreading it widely, usually with small fixtures recessed into the ceiling.
terms.simple_definition: Small ceiling lights that point light at a specific spot.

terms.definition: The lowest stone at each end of an arch, where the curve begins. It passes the arch's weight down to the wall or pier below.
terms.simple_definition: The bottom stone where an arch starts to curve.

terms.definition: A patterned window or panel made of colored glass pieces joined with lead strips. Common in Gothic cathedrals, it colors the light and gives a space atmosphere.
terms.simple_definition: A window made of pieces of colored glass that form a picture.

terms.definition: The sloping beam running along the side or underneath a staircase that carries the steps.
terms.simple_definition: The sloping side piece of a staircase that holds up the steps.

terms.definition: A building system whose load-bearing columns, beams and connections are made of steel sections. It is quick to erect, light and can span large distances.
terms.simple_definition: Building with a strong skeleton made of steel.

terms.definition: Each stage of a staircase, made up of the horizontal surface you step on (tread) and the vertical face between treads (riser).
terms.simple_definition: Each flat part of a staircase that you step on.

terms.definition: A reinforcing bar bent into a closed loop that wraps the long bars in concrete columns and beams. It holds them in place and keeps the member from bursting apart, especially in earthquakes.
terms.simple_definition: Steel loops that wrap around the bars inside a column.
