terms.definition: A long covered gallery in ancient Greek cities, usually along the edge of the agora (market square), open at the front with a row of columns and closed at the back by a wall. It was used for shade, meetings and trade.
terms.simple_definition: A long, roofed, column-lined walkway beside an ancient Greek market square.

terms.definition: Thin slabs of natural or manufactured stone fixed to a building's facade or interior walls. It gives the look of a stone building and protects against the weather.
terms.simple_definition: Thin stone slabs fixed to a wall to give it a stone look.

terms.definition: Fixed or movable horizontal or vertical fins on a façade that block direct sunlight without cutting off air or views.
terms.simple_definition: Slats on a building's face that block the sun but let air through.

terms.definition: A second ceiling of plasterboard or panels hung on rods below the main ceiling. It hides cables, pipes and ducts and makes it easy to fit recessed lights.
terms.simple_definition: A second ceiling hung below the real one to hide cables and pipes.

terms.definition: The principle of designing, building and running buildings so they use resources such as energy, water and materials efficiently and cause as little harm as possible to nature and future generations.
terms.simple_definition: Building in a way that does not waste resources or harm nature.

terms.definition: When the parts on either side of a central line through a building or layout are identical or mirror images of each other. In classical architecture it creates a sense of order and balance.
terms.simple_definition: When the left and right sides of a building match each other.

terms.definition: A woodworking joint where a projection left on the end of one piece (the tenon) fits into a matching hole (the mortise) in another. It joins two pieces of wood firmly without nails or screws.
terms.simple_definition: A wood joint where a peg on one piece fits into a hole in another.

terms.definition: A flat, open-air outdoor area on a building's roof or at ground level beside it. It is used for sitting, relaxing or as a garden.
terms.simple_definition: A large flat outdoor area on a roof or next to a building.

terms.definition: Similar-looking houses built in a row, each sharing its side walls with its neighbors. Each house usually has its own entrance and a small garden.
terms.simple_definition: Houses built side by side in a row, sharing their side walls.

terms.definition: A strip of stone, wood or metal at the bottom of a doorway that joins two floor finishes or keeps water out.
terms.simple_definition: The strip at the bottom of a doorway that you step over.

terms.definition: A thin, glazed, easy-to-clean ceramic tile used to cover bathroom and kitchen walls.
terms.simple_definition: The shiny ceramic tiles on bathroom and kitchen walls.

terms.definition: Wood that has been dried and processed for building and furniture, used in structures, floors, doors and windows, and cladding.
terms.simple_definition: Wood prepared for building houses and furniture.

terms.definition: A traditional building method with stone or brick (masonry) lower floors and timber-framed upper floors, very common in old Turkish houses.
terms.simple_definition: A house with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors.

terms.definition: A ladder-shaped bathroom radiator that both holds towels and heats the room.
terms.simple_definition: A warm ladder-shaped radiator for drying towels in the bathroom.

terms.definition: Spotlights mounted on a track fixed to the ceiling or wall, which can be slid along it and aimed in any direction. It gives flexible lighting in shops, galleries and kitchens.
terms.simple_definition: Lights on a ceiling rail that can be slid along and turned.

terms.definition: Building traditions shaped over generations by a region's climate, local materials and way of life; the houses of Safranbolu and Mardin are well-known examples.
terms.simple_definition: Old local ways of building with local materials.

terms.definition: A stepped ceiling whose central section is higher than its edges, like an upside-down tray. Hidden LED strip lighting is often fitted in the step around the edge.
terms.simple_definition: A ceiling whose middle part is raised higher than its edges, like an upside-down tray.

terms.definition: A staircase that turns 180 degrees at a middle landing and continues in the opposite direction, forming a U. It is the most common type in apartment buildings.
terms.simple_definition: A staircase that turns right back on itself halfway, like the letter U.

terms.definition: The floor area of a flat or building that can actually be used, excluding wall thicknesses; it is smaller than the gross area.
terms.simple_definition: The floor space you can actually use, not counting the walls.

terms.definition: A curved covering built from stone or brick on the principle of the arch, laid side by side. It roofs a space without needing columns; types include barrel, groin and ribbed vaults.
terms.simple_definition: A curved stone or brick roof or ceiling shaped like a tunnel.

terms.definition: A ceiling that curves or rises following the roof slope instead of being flat. It makes a room feel more open and tall; in modern homes it is usually a non-structural interior finish.
terms.simple_definition: A high ceiling that curves or slopes upward instead of being flat.

terms.definition: A window blind made of thin horizontal slats that can be tilted to control light and privacy.
terms.simple_definition: A window blind of thin strips that you can tilt.

terms.definition: A facade system with an air gap between the building's wall and its outer cladding. Air moving through the gap carries moisture away and helps keep the building cooler in summer and warmer in winter.
terms.simple_definition: A building skin with an air gap behind it that lets the wall breathe.

terms.definition: A roofed sitting area attached to a building's outer wall, open or glazed at the sides. Overlooking the garden, it is a transition zone between inside and outside.
terms.simple_definition: A roofed sitting area on the side of a house that looks onto the garden.

terms.definition: A small entrance hall between a building's outer door and its interior. It also acts as a buffer that reduces heat loss and drafts.
terms.simple_definition: The small entry area you pass through right after the front door.

terms.definition: A long bridge standing on many piers or arches, built to carry a road or railway over a deep valley, river or built-up area.
terms.simple_definition: A long, tall bridge on many supports that crosses a valley.

terms.definition: The scenery seen from a building's windows, balcony or terrace. In architectural design, room orientation and window positions are often chosen to capture the best view.
terms.simple_definition: What you can see outside from a window or balcony.

terms.definition: Showing a design as realistic 3D computer images before it is built, so materials, lighting and furniture choices can be seen in advance.
terms.simple_definition: A computer picture showing how a space will look before it is built.

terms.definition: In architecture, the three-dimensional size of a building or space and how its mass is perceived from outside; designers compose buildings as combinations of volumes.
terms.simple_definition: The 3D space a building or room takes up.

terms.definition: Covering the lower part of a wall, up to a certain height, with wood, MDF or marble panels. It protects the wall and gives the room a classic look.
terms.simple_definition: Wood or stone panels covering the lower part of a wall.

terms.definition: A small room, usually off the bedroom, large enough to walk into, where clothes and accessories are kept on shelves and rails.
terms.simple_definition: A room-sized wardrobe you can walk into.

terms.definition: A vertical building element that encloses or divides a space; load-bearing walls also carry the building's weight, while partition walls only separate areas.
terms.simple_definition: The upright structure that closes in a house or separates rooms.

terms.definition: Fixing thin strips of wood, polyurethane or MDF to a wall to create rectangular frames or patterns. It adds depth and a classic feel to a plain wall.
terms.simple_definition: Thin strips stuck to a wall to make decorative frames.

terms.definition: A recess cut into a wall or formed while building it, used for shelves, ornaments or lighting.
terms.simple_definition: A hollow in a wall for displaying objects.

terms.definition: A light fitting mounted on a wall rather than the ceiling, usually giving indirect or decorative light.
terms.simple_definition: A lamp fixed to the wall.

terms.definition: A large cupboard with doors in which clothes are hung or folded; it can be freestanding or built into the wall.
terms.simple_definition: A big cupboard for hanging clothes.

terms.definition: Stopping water and moisture from getting into a building at points such as foundations, roofs, terraces and bathrooms, using membranes, coatings and careful detailing. It extends a building's life and prevents damp.
terms.simple_definition: Keeping rain and moisture from leaking into a building.

terms.definition: The horizontal slab of stone, marble, wood or metal at the bottom edge of a window, inside or outside. The outer sill throws rainwater away from the wall.
terms.simple_definition: The narrow shelf at the bottom of a window.

terms.definition: A room with no window to the outside, so it gets no daylight and needs artificial lighting and mechanical ventilation; often used for storage or dressing.
terms.simple_definition: A room with no windows and no daylight.

terms.definition: A comfortable upholstered armchair with a high back and side 'wings' that support the head.
terms.simple_definition: A comfy armchair with a tall back and side wings for your head.

terms.definition: A room with glass walls, and often a glass roof, where plants are kept through winter and people can sit in the sun even in cold months.
terms.simple_definition: A glass room for plants where you can sit in the sun in winter.

terms.definition: The edge of a roof that projects beyond the outer wall. It protects walls and windows from rain and summer sun.
terms.simple_definition: The edge of a roof that sticks out past the wall, like the brim of a hat.

terms.definition: The craft of heating and hammering iron into curved, decorative shapes, and the railings, gates and window grilles made this way.
terms.simple_definition: Decorative curly ironwork used for railings and gates.

terms.definition: A large built-in wall cupboard in traditional Turkish houses where mattresses, quilts and pillows were stored during the day. It often also contained a small washing cubicle.
terms.simple_definition: A big built-in wall cupboard where bedding was kept in old Turkish houses.

terms.definition: A stepped, tower-like temple structure built in ancient Mesopotamia, made of progressively smaller levels. A small shrine usually stood on top.
terms.simple_definition: A huge ancient temple shaped like a stepped pyramid.

terms.definition: The top floor of a building built set back from the facade line of the floors below, usually leaving a terrace in front of it. Whether it is allowed, and its dimensions, are set by the zoning plan and building regulations.
terms.simple_definition: A top floor pulled back from the building's front so that a terrace is left in front of it.

terms.definition: A window unit made of two panes of glass sealed together at the edges with a gap of air or special gas between them. Compared with a single pane it greatly reduces heat loss and outside noise.
terms.simple_definition: A window with two layers of glass and a gap between them, keeping the home warmer and quieter.

terms.definition: A decorative ceramic tile made from a clay-based body that is painted with patterns, glazed and fired at high temperature. Tiles from Iznik are the best-known example, used widely to clad walls in Seljuk and Ottoman buildings.
terms.simple_definition: A traditional Turkish glazed tile with painted patterns, used to decorate walls.

terms.definition: A water structure built into a wall or standing on its own that delivers running water from a tap or spout for public use. Charitable Ottoman fountains, with their inscriptions and carvings, are important pieces of city architecture.
terms.simple_definition: A public spot in a street or wall where running water flows for everyone to use.

terms.definition: An open area on top of a flat roof that is fitted out for sitting, gardening or relaxing. It needs careful detailing of waterproofing, drainage and guard rails.
terms.simple_definition: An open terrace on top of a flat roof where you can sit and spend time.

terms.definition: A small utility room with water and drain connections set aside for the washing machine, dryer, ironing and cleaning supplies. As a wet area, its floor and walls should be water-resistant.
terms.simple_definition: A small room in the home for washing, drying and ironing clothes.

terms.definition: A room in a home set aside for desk work, reading or studying, ideally well lit and kept quiet. It is often used as a home office.
terms.simple_definition: A quiet room in the home used for working or reading.

terms.definition: A split that forms in plaster, concrete, walls or slabs when the material separates under stress. Hairline cracks are often only cosmetic, but wide, diagonal or growing cracks can signal a structural problem and should be checked by an expert.
terms.simple_definition: A thin split that appears in a wall, plaster or concrete.

terms.definition: A metal covering for roofs and facades made of zinc sheets joined with folded seams. It is long-lasting and forms a matte grey protective layer (patina) over time.
terms.simple_definition: Long-lasting zinc metal sheets used to cover a roof or wall.

terms.definition: Diagonal members, usually steel, fixed corner to corner across a frame of columns and beams in an X shape. They stop the structure from racking under sideways forces such as wind and earthquakes.
terms.simple_definition: Bars set in an X shape across a frame to stop a building from swaying.

terms.definition: A triangular timber roof frame in which two vertical posts connect the sloping rafters to the horizontal tie beam below. It can span wider openings than a king post truss.
terms.simple_definition: A wooden triangular roof frame with two upright posts in the middle.

terms.definition: The required open distance between a building's front facade and the plot boundary facing the street. In Türkiye it is at least 5 metres under the Planned Areas Zoning Regulation unless the zoning plan says otherwise.
terms.simple_definition: The distance that must be left empty between a building and the street in front.

terms.definition: Concrete elements cast and cured in moulds at a factory, then transported to site and assembled, instead of being poured in place. It offers easier quality control and faster construction.
terms.simple_definition: Concrete pieces made in a factory and brought to the site ready to install.

terms.definition: The permanent, unchanging load made up of the structure's own weight and fixed elements such as walls, finishes and services. Engineers combine it with live loads, like people and furniture, when designing the structure.
terms.simple_definition: The weight of the building itself and everything permanently fixed to it.

terms.definition: A fully furnished and decorated sample apartment prepared to show buyers the quality and layout of a project before purchase. It is usually set up on site or next to the sales office.
terms.simple_definition: A furnished sample apartment that shows buyers what the finished home will look like.

terms.definition: A building whose parts, such as walls, floors or whole room modules, are made in a factory and assembled on site. It goes up quickly and its quality is easier to control.
terms.simple_definition: A building made of factory-built parts that are put together on site.

terms.definition: The pattern in which bricks or stones are laid and staggered in a wall. A proper bond keeps vertical joints from lining up, which makes the wall stronger and gives the facade its texture.
terms.simple_definition: The pattern in which bricks are stacked to build a wall.

terms.definition: In conservation and restoration, the degree to which a building keeps its original materials, techniques, form and historical traces. International conservation principles require that interventions do not destroy it.
terms.simple_definition: How true a historic building has stayed to its original state.

terms.definition: Showing sizes such as wall thicknesses, room dimensions and door and window widths on architectural drawings using dimension lines and figures. Drawings must be fully dimensioned so builders can construct them correctly.
terms.simple_definition: Writing the measurements of everything on a drawing.

terms.definition: A cement-based layer poured over the structural concrete slab to level it and prepare it for final finishes such as parquet or tiles. Underfloor heating pipes are often embedded in it.
terms.simple_definition: A thin layer of cement poured to level a floor before the final covering.

terms.definition: The sloping face left at an excavation or fill so that the soil stays stable without sliding. Its angle depends on the soil type, and it may be supported by a retaining wall if needed.
terms.simple_definition: A sloped bank of earth shaped so that it doesn't slide.

terms.definition: The enclosed work area where a building is being constructed, with its materials, machinery and workers. Safety signage, site safety measures and a site manager are legally required.
terms.simple_definition: The place where a building is being built.

terms.definition: An enclosed vertical void running through the floors of a building that carries water, drainage, electrical and ventilation lines. It must be accessible for maintenance and protected against fire.
terms.simple_definition: A vertical channel that carries pipes and cables between floors.

terms.definition: The discipline of organising a city's land use, building density, transport, infrastructure and green spaces over the long term. In Türkiye it is put into practice through regional, master and implementation zoning plans.
terms.simple_definition: Planning in advance what gets built where in a city.

terms.definition: An open hearth built against or into a wall, with a chimney, burning wood or gas. Beyond heating, it acts as a strong decorative focal point in a living room.
terms.simple_definition: An open place in a wall with a chimney where a fire is lit.

terms.definition: A simple tool made of a weight hung on a string, which shows a true vertical line thanks to gravity. It is used to check that walls, columns and frames are perfectly upright.
terms.simple_definition: A weight on a string used to check that a wall is perfectly upright.

terms.definition: A continuous foundation running beneath walls or a row of columns, spreading their load into the ground along a wide strip. It is common in masonry and low-rise buildings.
terms.simple_definition: A long strip of foundation running underneath the walls.

terms.definition: A written document describing the quality of materials, construction methods and standards required for building work. Together with the drawings it forms part of the contract and is referred to in disputes.
terms.simple_definition: A document that says which materials to use and how the work should be done.

terms.definition: The narrow balcony with a railing that runs around the shaft of a minaret. Traditionally it is where the muezzin calls to prayer, and the number of balconies reflects the mosque's importance.
terms.simple_definition: The small balcony that wraps around a minaret.

terms.definition: The part of a building above its foundations, made up of columns, beams, slabs and walls. At city scale the term refers to buildings and facilities that sit on top of infrastructure.
terms.simple_definition: The part of a building above the foundations that you can see.

terms.definition: A window unit made of three panes of glass with two sealed gaps between them. It insulates against heat loss and noise better than double glazing and is preferred in cold climates and energy-efficient buildings.
terms.simple_definition: A window with three layers of glass that insulates very well.

terms.definition: Kitchen cabinets hung on the wall above the worktop. Together with base cabinets they provide the kitchen's storage, usually with about 55–65 cm of clearance above the counter.
terms.simple_definition: Kitchen cupboards hung on the wall above the counter.

terms.definition: A bridge-like structure that carries pedestrians or vehicles over a road, railway or junction. It allows safe crossing without interrupting traffic below.
terms.simple_definition: A bridge built to cross over a road.

terms.definition: In architecture and urbanism, imaginary designs for cities and buildings in which society would live in an ideal order. Even when never built, utopian projects deeply influenced city planning and modern architecture.
terms.simple_definition: An imagined perfect city or building designed for an ideal way of life.

terms.definition: A plan covering a large area, such as a regional plan or environmental plan, that guides the more detailed master and implementation zoning plans beneath it. Lower-tier plans may not contradict it.
terms.simple_definition: A large-area plan that sets the rules for the more detailed city plans.

terms.definition: A volumetric model of a building or interior created on a computer or as a physical maquette. It lets clients see a design from every angle and make decisions before construction.
terms.simple_definition: A virtual or physical model of a building or room you can see from all sides.

terms.definition: The continuous member forming the upper edge of a truss, usually working in compression. Together with the bottom chord and the posts and diagonals between them, it carries loads to the supports.
terms.simple_definition: The long piece along the top of a roof truss.

terms.definition: The official permission issued by the municipality or governorship to construct, extend or substantially alter a building. It is granted once the approved drawings are found to comply with zoning law; building without it is illegal.
terms.simple_definition: Official permission from the municipality needed before starting to build.

terms.definition: In Türkiye, the checking of construction by licensed supervision firms, from the drawings through to the occupancy permit, to make sure the work follows the approved design, standards and regulations. Concrete pours, reinforcement and material tests are part of it.
terms.simple_definition: An independent firm checking that a building is being built by the rules.

terms.definition: A vertical pipe that carries rainwater collected in the roof gutters down to the ground or a stormwater drain. If it clogs, damp problems can appear on the facade and foundations.
terms.simple_definition: A vertical pipe that brings rainwater down from the roof.

terms.definition: Heating a room from the floor using hot-water pipes or electric cables laid within the floor, usually under the screed. It spreads heat evenly and frees walls because no radiators are needed.
terms.simple_definition: A heating system under the floor that warms the room without radiators.

terms.definition: A self-closing door built to hold back fire and smoke for a rated period, such as 30, 60 or 90 minutes. Regulations require it at stairwells, car parks and plant rooms.
terms.simple_definition: A special door that holds back fire and smoke for a set time.

terms.definition: A building system in which loads are carried to the ground by walls built of stone, brick or blocks rather than by a frame of columns and beams. It is common in traditional houses, and earthquake codes limit its number of floors and wall layout.
terms.simple_definition: A building held up by thick stone or brick walls instead of columns.

terms.definition: A roof planted with vegetation over layers of waterproofing, root barrier, drainage and soil. It insulates the building, holds back rainwater and reduces the urban heat island effect.
terms.simple_definition: A roof covered with plants and grass.

terms.definition: A large, often timber mansion built right on the water's edge, especially along the Bosphorus in Istanbul. Yalıs are among the best-known examples of Ottoman residential architecture.
terms.simple_definition: A large historic waterside house built right on the Bosphorus shore.

terms.definition: The outermost line a building may reach on its plot once the required front, side and rear setbacks have been left. The building may not cross it; the area inside it is where construction is allowed.
terms.simple_definition: The line on a plot that a building is not allowed to go beyond.

terms.definition: In Turkish regulations, generally a building whose height exceeds 21.50 metres (or whose total structure height exceeds 30.50 metres). Such buildings are subject to extra rules for fire safety, seismic design and evacuation.
terms.simple_definition: A tall building that must follow stricter safety rules because of its height.

terms.definition: A window in which one or both sashes slide sideways along a track to open. Because the sash does not swing in or out, it is practical in tight spaces; the traditional English version is called a Yorkshire light.
terms.simple_definition: A window that opens by sliding sideways.

terms.definition: A traditional Japanese technique in which the surface of timber is deliberately charred, then brushed and oiled. It protects the wood against moisture, insects and sun and gives it a dark, textured look; also known as shou sugi ban.
terms.simple_definition: Wood cladding that is burnt on purpose to make it dark and long-lasting.

terms.definition: A round, portable tent-house of Central Asian nomadic culture, made of a wooden lattice frame covered with felt and easily taken down and moved. It is an early example of portable architecture built from local materials.
terms.simple_definition: A round felt-covered tent home used by nomads.

terms.definition: A traditional mud-brick structure from Iran, with a tall dome over an underground store, used to make and keep ice in the desert climate. It is a famous example of passive cooling without electricity.
terms.simple_definition: An ancient domed building used to store ice in the desert without electricity.

terms.definition: Stone bars in Gothic architecture that branch in a Y shape to divide the upper part of a window opening in two. It is one of the earliest and simplest forms of tracery.
terms.simple_definition: Stone bars in a Gothic window that divide the glass in a Y shape.

terms.definition: A section of road marked with stripes where pedestrians can cross safely. In urban design it is a basic element of walkability and accessibility.
terms.simple_definition: A striped place on the road where people can cross safely.

terms.definition: The storey of a building at or nearest to street or natural ground level, where the entrance usually is. Zoning rules treat it as the reference level between basements and upper floors.
terms.simple_definition: The floor of a building at street level, where you usually enter.

terms.definition: Strengthening soil that has low bearing capacity or a liquefaction risk, using methods such as jet grouting, bored piles, stone columns or injection. It is done before the foundations when the soil survey calls for it.
terms.simple_definition: Making weak ground stronger before a building is built on it.

terms.definition: The loss of strength in loose, water-saturated sandy soils during earthquake shaking, causing them to behave like a liquid. Because it can make buildings sink or tilt, it must be assessed in the soil survey.
terms.simple_definition: When wet ground turns almost liquid in an earthquake and can no longer hold a building.

terms.definition: The downward movement of a building as the soil beneath it compresses over time under its load. When parts settle by different amounts, cracks in walls and sticking doors and windows can result.
terms.simple_definition: When the ground squeezes under a building's weight and the building sinks slightly.

terms.definition: The classification of ground in the Turkish Building Earthquake Code from ZA (hard rock) to ZF (weak soils needing special study), based on how it behaves in earthquakes. This class directly affects the building's seismic design.
terms.simple_definition: A grade that shows how firm the ground under a building is in an earthquake.

terms.definition: A small lodge in the Seljuk and early Ottoman periods where dervishes lived and travellers were given food and shelter. It is the origin of the early Ottoman zawiya-type (inverted-T plan) mosques.
terms.simple_definition: A small historic lodge where dervishes lived and travellers were fed.

terms.definition: Smoothing and levelling a wood, plaster or painted surface by abrading it with sandpaper. It is a key step in refinishing parquet and preparing surfaces before painting.
terms.simple_definition: Rubbing a surface with sandpaper to make it smooth.

terms.definition: The maximum load per unit area that the ground can safely carry without excessive settlement or failure. It is found in the soil survey, and foundation sizes are calculated from it.
terms.simple_definition: The most weight the ground can safely carry.

terms.definition: Mosaic tilework from Moroccan and Andalusian architecture in which small hand-cut pieces of glazed terracotta are set in geometric patterns. Today it is popular on kitchen and bathroom walls for its handmade texture.
terms.simple_definition: Moroccan mosaic made of small hand-cut coloured tiles.

terms.definition: A Japanese dry garden of rocks, raked sand or gravel, moss and a few plants, designed for simplicity and calm. It is used as a meditative landscape in courtyards and small gardens.
terms.simple_definition: A calm, simple Japanese garden made of stones, sand and few plants.

terms.definition: A pattern of broken lines repeated in a row of V shapes. It is common in parquet flooring, tiling, and Romanesque and Art Deco ornament.
terms.simple_definition: A pattern of repeating V-shaped lines.

terms.definition: Bringing daylight into a space directly from above through roof windows, skylights or ceiling openings. It gives even, soft light in deep-plan spaces and museums.
terms.simple_definition: Lighting a room with daylight coming in from openings in the ceiling.

terms.definition: Dividing urban land in zoning plans into use zones such as residential, commercial, industrial and green space, and setting building rules for each. It determines what can be built on each plot and at what density.
terms.simple_definition: Deciding which parts of a city are for homes, shops, factories or parks.

terms.definition: The detailed set of drawings prepared after the preliminary design is approved, containing all the dimensions, materials and details needed to build the project. Permits and on-site work are based on them.
terms.simple_definition: The final, fully detailed drawings used to actually build the building.

terms.definition: A lightweight three-dimensional structure made of struts joined at nodes to form a grid. It is used to span large areas such as sports halls, exhibition centres and hangars without intermediate columns.
terms.simple_definition: A 3D grid of connected bars that holds up large roofs without columns.

terms.definition: The largest and main congregational mosque of a city, where Friday prayers are held. Seljuk and early Ottoman examples, such as those in Bursa and Divriği, have wide prayer halls with many supports.
terms.simple_definition: The largest and most important mosque of a city.

terms.definition: A new settlement planned around a large city, linked to it but with its own housing, jobs and services. It is created to reduce population pressure on the main city.
terms.simple_definition: A new town built near a big city that has its own homes and services.

terms.definition: An early 20th-century movement in Türkiye that combined Ottoman and Seljuk elements such as arches, domes and tiles with modern construction techniques. Vedat Tek and Architect Kemaleddin were its leading figures.
terms.simple_definition: A Turkish style that used Ottoman and Seljuk decoration on modern buildings.

terms.definition: The line and profile that a city's buildings form against the sky when seen from a distance. It is an important consideration in decisions about tall buildings and in protecting historic cities.
terms.simple_definition: The outline of a city's buildings against the sky seen from far away.

terms.definition: An experienced worker who leads the tradespeople and labourers of a particular trade on site and oversees daily planning and quality. The foreman acts as a link between the site manager and the workers.
terms.simple_definition: The experienced worker who leads the other workers on a building site.

terms.definition: Planning a city's roads, public transport, cycling and pedestrian networks to meet its needs. Considered together with land use, it aims to reduce traffic and improve access.
terms.simple_definition: Planning how people will get around a city.

terms.definition: A value showing how much heat passes through a wall, roof or window per unit area per degree of temperature difference (W/m²K). The lower the value, the better the insulation.
terms.simple_definition: A number that shows how much heat escapes through a wall or window.

terms.definition: A thin sheet or membrane placed within wall, roof or floor layers to stop indoor water vapour from passing into the insulation and condensing. It is usually placed on the warm (inner) side of the insulation.
terms.simple_definition: A thin layer that stops indoor moisture from getting inside walls and causing mould.

terms.definition: A plan, usually at 1:5000 scale, showing a city's general land uses, densities, main transport network and directions of growth. It forms the basis of the more detailed implementation zoning plans.
terms.simple_definition: The main zoning plan showing how a city will grow overall.

terms.definition: A reinforced concrete floor made of a thin slab with closely spaced small beams (ribs) running underneath. It spans wide openings with less concrete; the spaces between ribs are often filled with hollow blocks.
terms.simple_definition: A lighter concrete floor with many small beams underneath.

terms.definition: A reference point fixed on the ground with a concrete block or metal marker, whose position and height are precisely known, used in mapping and cadastral surveys. Plot boundaries and building setting-out are measured from it.
terms.simple_definition: A fixed point with an exactly known location that surveyors measure from.

terms.definition: A style from the late 18th century onward, especially in England, that revived medieval Gothic elements such as pointed arches, stained glass and spires. It was widely used for churches, universities and parliament buildings; also called Gothic Revival.
terms.simple_definition: A later style that copied the pointed-arch Gothic look of the Middle Ages.

terms.definition: The zoning rule for how buildings sit on their plots relative to neighbours: detached buildings have gardens on all sides, attached buildings share a wall with their neighbours, and block arrangement joins several buildings into one block.
terms.simple_definition: The rule that says whether a building stands alone or is joined to its neighbours.

terms.definition: Samples taken during a concrete pour and cured in cube or cylinder moulds, then crushed in a laboratory to measure their strength. Building inspection uses them to confirm the concrete meets the specified class.
terms.simple_definition: A small sample of concrete tested to check how strong it is.

terms.definition: Wetness in building elements caused by water rising from the ground, leaking in from rain or condensing indoors. It leads to mould, blistering paint and crumbling plaster and is fixed with waterproofing or ventilation depending on its source.
terms.simple_definition: Wetness in walls that causes mould and peeling paint.

terms.definition: The actual usable floor area of a flat measured between the inner faces of its walls. It excludes wall thicknesses and any share of common areas, so it is smaller than the gross area.
terms.simple_definition: The floor space inside a home that you can actually use.

terms.definition: The long central part of a church or basilica running from the entrance towards the apse, where the congregation gathers. It is usually separated from the side aisles by rows of columns.
terms.simple_definition: The long main hall of a church from the entrance to the front.

terms.definition: The entrance hall running across the width of a Byzantine church, passed through before entering the main space. Hagia Sophia has two, an inner and an outer narthex.
terms.simple_definition: The entrance hall you pass through before the main hall of an old church.

terms.definition: A building with very low energy demand that covers part of that demand with renewable energy produced on site, such as solar panels. In Türkiye the Energy Performance of Buildings Regulation requires it for new buildings above a certain size.
terms.simple_definition: A building that uses very little energy and makes some of its own.

terms.definition: The thick vertical post at the start, end or turns of a staircase that supports the handrail. It is often decorated with a carved or turned cap.
terms.simple_definition: The thick upright post at the bottom or top of a stair railing.

terms.definition: The front edge of a stair tread that projects slightly beyond the riser below. It gives the foot more room, and a non-slip profile improves safety.
terms.simple_definition: The front edge of a stair step that sticks out slightly.

terms.definition: A planning unit for a residential area in which daily needs such as a primary school, park and local shops are within walking distance. Developed in the early 20th century, it underpins pedestrian-scale neighbourhood design.
terms.simple_definition: A neighbourhood planned so that school, park and shops are within walking distance.

terms.definition: Reducing the passage of sound from one space to another using dense materials, resilient layers and air gaps in walls, floors and windows. It is important for blocking noise between flats and from outside traffic.
terms.simple_definition: Stopping sound from passing between rooms or homes.

terms.definition: An open area or covered floors set aside for parking vehicles. Under Türkiye's Parking Regulation, new buildings must provide a set number of spaces based on their number of homes or businesses.
terms.simple_definition: An area or floor where cars are parked.

terms.definition: The shared room in a home where the family sits and relaxes day to day, watches television and receives guests. It can be combined with or separate from a formal lounge.
terms.simple_definition: The room where the family sits and spends time together.

terms.definition: The direction a building and its rooms face in relation to sun, wind, views and streets. Good orientation increases daylight and lowers heating and cooling costs.
terms.simple_definition: Which way a building and its rooms face towards the sun and view.

terms.definition: The parts of an apartment building or complex used jointly by all owners, such as the entrance hall, stairs, lift, roof, car park and garden. Under Turkish condominium law they are jointly owned and their costs are shared.
terms.simple_definition: Parts of a building everyone shares, like stairs and the garden.

terms.definition: An approach that designs buildings in harmony with their natural setting and site, using natural materials and flowing forms. Frank Lloyd Wright's Fallingwater is its best-known example.
terms.simple_definition: Designing buildings to blend in with nature as if they were part of it.

terms.definition: The architectural tradition that developed across Ottoman lands from the 14th to the early 20th century, known for central-domed mosques, külliye complexes, inns and timber houses. Mimar Sinan is its greatest master.
terms.simple_definition: The architecture of the Ottoman era, known for domed mosques and timber houses.

terms.definition: A half-pipe channel running along the edge of the roof eaves that collects rainwater and directs it to the downpipes. If not cleaned regularly it can overflow and damage the facade and foundations.
terms.simple_definition: A channel along the roof edge that catches rainwater.

terms.definition: A wall on the plot boundary that separates two neighbouring attached buildings. It must meet special fire and sound insulation requirements.
terms.simple_definition: A wall shared by two buildings next to each other.

terms.definition: Designed open areas outside the building, such as gardens, terraces, courtyards and balconies. With landscaping, shading and outdoor furniture they can work as an extension of the interior.
terms.simple_definition: Areas outside the building that people use, like gardens and terraces.

terms.definition: A layout in which functions such as living, dining and kitchen are combined in one large space without dividing walls. It makes the home feel brighter and more spacious.
terms.simple_definition: A layout where the living room, kitchen and dining area share one space with no walls.

terms.definition: A tall, single-piece stone monument with a square section that tapers upwards and ends in a pyramid-shaped top. The Obelisk of Theodosius in Istanbul's Sultanahmet Square is a well-known example.
terms.simple_definition: A tall pointed stone pillar made from a single piece.

terms.definition: An arch made of two S-shaped curves, each combining a concave and a convex part, meeting at a pointed top. It is common in late Gothic architecture and Ottoman decoration.
terms.simple_definition: An arch with S-shaped sides that meet in a point at the top.

terms.definition: A home that meets its own needs without connecting to electricity, water or sewer networks, using solar panels, batteries, rainwater harvesting and on-site treatment.
terms.simple_definition: A home that makes its own power and water without being connected to city supplies.

terms.definition: A wall covering made of paper, vinyl or textile, produced in patterned or textured rolls and pasted onto walls. It offers richer patterns and textures than paint.
terms.simple_definition: A patterned paper covering glued onto walls.

terms.definition: All the timber, PVC or aluminium frames, sashes and leaves of a building's windows and doors. Joinery quality directly affects heat and sound insulation.
terms.simple_definition: The frames and opening parts of a building's windows and doors.

terms.definition: A non-load-bearing wall that fills the spaces between columns and beams in a concrete or steel frame. It is built from lightweight materials such as brick, aerated concrete or pumice blocks.
terms.simple_definition: A wall that fills the gaps in a building's frame but doesn't hold it up.

terms.definition: A home spread over two floors connected by its own internal staircase. Usually the living areas are downstairs and the bedrooms upstairs.
terms.simple_definition: A two-storey apartment with its own staircase inside.

terms.definition: An appliance mounted above the cooktop that draws in steam, smoke and odours from cooking and either vents them outside or filters them. It is both a functional and decorative element in kitchen design.
terms.simple_definition: The appliance above the cooker that sucks up cooking smells and steam.

terms.definition: The system of stairs, lifts and ramps that moves people between floors of a building. Its position and size are key planning decisions for ease of use and fire safety.
terms.simple_definition: How people move between floors using stairs and lifts.

terms.definition: Updating an existing building or space by changing partitions, services, finishes and fittings. Renovations affecting the structure or exterior require a renovation permit from the municipality.
terms.simple_definition: Changing and updating an existing home.

terms.definition: All the pipes, cables and equipment of a building's water, drainage, heating, ventilation, gas and electrical systems. They are designed in separate mechanical and electrical drawings.
terms.simple_definition: The pipes and cables for water, electricity, gas and heating in a building.

terms.definition: The combination of foundations, columns, beams, shear walls and slabs that carries a building's own weight, its contents and forces such as earthquakes and wind down to the ground. Load-bearing elements must not be altered during renovations.
terms.simple_definition: The columns, beams and foundations that hold a building up.

terms.definition: The ratio of the building's ground footprint to the plot area. For example, with a ratio of 0.30 on a 1,000 m² plot, the footprint can be at most 300 m²; the value is set in the zoning plan.
terms.simple_definition: The share of a plot that a building is allowed to cover.

terms.definition: The ratio of the total floor area that may be built on a plot to the plot area. For example, a ratio of 1.50 on a 500 m² plot allows at most 750 m² of countable floor area.
terms.simple_definition: The ratio that tells how much total floor space can be built on a plot.

terms.definition: The structural part at the very bottom of a building that safely transfers its whole load into the ground. Depending on the soil survey it is designed as pad, strip, raft (covering the whole area) or piled foundations.
terms.simple_definition: The bottom part of a building that passes all its weight into the ground.

terms.definition: A rectangular building unit made by moulding clay and firing it in a kiln. Solid and perforated types exist; bricks are used to build walls and as decorative facade cladding.
terms.simple_definition: A rectangular block of baked clay used to build walls.

terms.definition: A shade cover of fabric or similar material, often retractable, fitted over a window, balcony or terrace. It blocks sun and light rain.
terms.simple_definition: A fabric shade over a window or balcony that can open and close.

terms.definition: Fitting out a space with furniture, lighting, textiles and accessories so it is ready to use. Interior design projects include a furnishing plan alongside the layout plan.
terms.simple_definition: Filling a space with furniture and items so it is ready to live in.

terms.definition: A durable, unglazed floor tile made by firing natural clay at high temperature, with warm red-brown tones. It is widely used in kitchens, terraces and country houses.
terms.simple_definition: A reddish, unglazed floor tile made of baked clay.

terms.definition: An open-pit site where natural stones such as marble, granite and limestone, and aggregates, are extracted from the ground. When choosing natural stone, the quarry it comes from determines its colour and texture.
terms.simple_definition: A place where natural stone is dug out of the ground.

terms.definition: A triangular timber roof frame in which two sloping rafters meet at the apex and a single central vertical post connects the apex to the tie beam below. It is used for small to medium roof spans.
terms.simple_definition: A wooden triangular roof frame with one upright post in the middle.

terms.definition: Deepening and strengthening the foundation of an existing building by adding new concrete or piles beneath it, because of settlement, soil problems or extra loads.
terms.simple_definition: Strengthening an existing building's foundation from underneath.

terms.definition: The process of demolishing and rebuilding, or upgrading, earthquake-vulnerable or run-down buildings and neighbourhoods. In Türkiye it is carried out under Law No. 6306 on the Transformation of Areas under Disaster Risk.
terms.simple_definition: Replacing old, unsafe buildings and neighbourhoods with new ones.

terms.definition: The low-density, unplanned and car-dependent spread of a city into surrounding farmland and natural areas. It increases infrastructure costs and transport problems.
terms.simple_definition: A city spreading outward in a scattered, unplanned way.

terms.definition: Designing spaces and products so that everyone, regardless of age, size or disability, can use them without special adaptation. Step-free entrances and wide doorways are typical examples.
terms.simple_definition: Designing spaces so that everyone, young, old or disabled, can use them easily.

terms.definition: Large dressed stones set at the corners of a building, often differing in size, texture or colour from the wall surface. They strengthen the corner and accentuate the facade.
terms.simple_definition: Large, eye-catching stones set at the corners of a building.

terms.definition: A clover-like ornamental motif of four rounded lobes arranged around a common centre. It is common in Gothic window tracery, balustrades and reliefs.
terms.simple_definition: A decorative shape like a four-leaf clover.

terms.definition: A square or rectangular open courtyard enclosed by buildings on all four sides. It is a common plan element of universities, monasteries, madrasas and inns.
terms.simple_definition: A square open courtyard surrounded by buildings on all four sides.

terms.definition: A kitchen or bathroom worktop made from engineered stone produced by pressing natural quartz particles with resins and pigments. It is non-porous and resistant to scratches and stains.
terms.simple_definition: A tough, easy-to-clean kitchen counter made from quartz stone.

terms.definition: Measuring and calculating from the drawings the quantities of each work item, such as concrete, masonry, plaster and paint. It is the basis of cost estimates, bills of quantities and progress payments.
terms.simple_definition: Calculating how much material and work a building project needs.

terms.definition: Timber cut from the log so that the growth rings are roughly perpendicular to the face of the board. It moves and warps less and shows a straight, tight grain, making it preferred for quality flooring and furniture.
terms.simple_definition: Wood cut in a special way so it stays straight and shows a fine grain.

terms.definition: A very hard, durable natural metamorphic stone formed when sandstone is transformed by heat and pressure. Its marble-like veining makes it popular for countertops, floors and facade cladding.
terms.simple_definition: A natural stone that looks like marble but is much harder.

terms.definition: A landscaping approach designed to use little water, relying on drought-tolerant native plants, mulch and efficient irrigation. It saves water in hot, dry climates.
terms.simple_definition: Garden design using plants that need very little water.

terms.definition: In ancient Greece, a long covered portico at a gymnasium used for exercise in bad weather; in Roman times, a tree-lined garden walk or terrace.
terms.simple_definition: A long covered walkway used in ancient times for exercise and strolling.

terms.definition: A rigid, closed-cell thermal insulation board made by melting polystyrene and forcing it through a die. It resists water and compression and is used especially for foundations, basement walls and flat terrace roofs.
terms.simple_definition: A rigid, water-resistant foam board used to insulate buildings.

terms.definition: The highest stress a material, especially reinforcing steel, can carry before it starts to deform permanently. Rebar grades (for example B420C) are defined by this value.
terms.simple_definition: The most force steel can take before it bends permanently.

terms.definition: A coefficient showing how much a material stretches or compresses under load, i.e. its stiffness. The higher the value, the less the material deforms under the same load; it is used in calculations for concrete and steel.
terms.simple_definition: A value that shows how much a material bends or stretches under load.

terms.definition: The side faces and surrounding frame of a door or window opening, made of stone, marble, plaster or timber. It protects the edge of the opening and adds decoration to the facade.
terms.simple_definition: The frame around the sides of a door or window opening.

terms.definition: Small beams laid parallel at close spacing in timber or steel floors to support the floor decking. They carry the load to main beams or walls.
terms.simple_definition: Thin beams laid side by side to hold up a floor.

terms.definition: An edging stone of concrete or stone that separates the pavement from the road, or a planted area from a path. It guides surface water and marks the boundary.
terms.simple_definition: The edge stone between the pavement and the road.

terms.definition: A covered underground chamber built where drainage and stormwater pipes meet, used for inspection and cleaning. Blockages are cleared through its cover.
terms.simple_definition: A covered pit in the ground used to check and clean drain pipes.

terms.definition: Covering a building's outer walls with insulation boards, then applying mesh and a decorative render on top. It reduces heat loss and condensation and lowers heating bills considerably.
terms.simple_definition: Wrapping a building's outside walls in insulation to keep heat in.

terms.definition: An open area enclosed by walls or buildings, within or in front of a building or group of buildings. It is the centre of daily life in traditional Turkish houses, mosques and inns.
terms.simple_definition: An open space surrounded by buildings or walls.

terms.definition: The area of a unit measured to its outer wall faces, including walls, plus its share of the common areas. The larger figure in property listings is usually the gross area.
terms.simple_definition: A home's total area including walls and its share of shared spaces.

terms.definition: A board made of gypsum pressed between two layers of paper, screwed onto metal studs to build partition walls and suspended ceilings. It is a fast, light, dry construction method.
terms.simple_definition: Light gypsum boards used to build interior walls and ceilings.

terms.definition: A vertical shaft left open to the sky, or covered with glass, that brings daylight and fresh air to inner rooms and stairs of a building.
terms.simple_definition: An open shaft inside a building that lets light and air reach inner rooms.

terms.definition: A spot where insulation is interrupted, such as at a column, beam or balcony slab, letting heat escape; it often causes cold walls, condensation and mould.
terms.simple_definition: A weak spot in insulation where a home's heat leaks outside.

terms.definition: The general name for rooms that come into contact with water, such as bathrooms, toilets, kitchens and laundries, where waterproofing and plumbing matter most.
terms.simple_definition: Rooms where water is used, such as bathrooms and kitchens.

terms.definition: A durable synthetic fabric used in groundworks, drainage and landscaping to separate layers, filter water and reinforce the soil.
terms.simple_definition: A special fabric laid in the ground that lets water through but holds soil in place.

terms.definition: A way of heating and cooling a building using the earth's natural underground warmth through heat pumps and pipes buried in the ground.
terms.simple_definition: Heating a home with the natural warmth found underground.

terms.definition: A window sash hinged at the bottom that tilts inward from the top, giving ventilation without opening fully.
terms.simple_definition: A window that tips inward at the top to let air in.

terms.definition: A cupboard or small room at the entrance where coats, umbrellas and shoes are left.
terms.simple_definition: A cupboard or small room by the door for coats.
